Yes. Set out 4 crepes, 1 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 bananas, and 1 (7 ounce) can of pressurized whipped cream. You'll also want a knife, spreading knife or spoon, and a skillet.
The bananas are still whole. Should I slice them before I start filling the crepes?
Slice all 4 bananas before assembling so the filling is ready to divide evenly. Each crepe gets 1 sliced banana.
I have the crepes laid flat on the counter. How much chocolate hazelnut spread goes on each one?
Spread 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread over each crepe. Aim for an even layer that reaches close to the edges without piling it up at the rim.
The spread is on. Where should the banana slices go so the crepes roll neatly?
Arrange 1 sliced banana in a line down the center of each crepe. Keeping the slices centered will make the rolls easier to close.
One banana is a little riper and softer than the others. Is it still okay to use?
Yes, use it as long as it can be sliced and arranged down the middle. Place the softest slices among firmer ones so the filling stays in a tidy line.
All four are filled. What is the best way to roll them before they go into the skillet?
Fold or tuck the crepe over the banana line, then roll it up into a compact cylinder. Place each roll seam-side down as you finish it.
My skillet is warming. What heat and timing should I use?
Put the rolled crepes into a warm skillet over medium heat and let them warm for about 90 seconds. They only need to heat through, not cook for a long time.
They've been in the skillet for about 90 seconds and feel warm. How should I serve them?
Transfer the warm crepes to plates and use the pressurized whipped cream as the topping. Serve while the chocolate hazelnut filling and bananas are warm.
I'm making Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me get the ingredients and pans ready?

Yes. Gather 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate. Chop the chocolate if it is not already chopped, and have 2 (9 inch) pans ready.
I have the flour, baking soda, salt, and chocolate on the counter. Should the oven be heating yet?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is ready while you prepare the pans and dry ingredients.
The oven is preheating. What is the best way to prepare the two pans?
Grease and flour both 9 inch pans. Coat the inside surfaces with grease, add flour, and turn each pan until the flour covers the greased areas; tap out any excess.
Both pans are coated, and the chocolate is chopped. Which ingredients go into the sifter?
Sift together the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. The chopped unsweetened chocolate stays separate at this point.
I only have a fine-mesh sieve rather than a traditional flour sifter. Is that okay?
A fine-mesh sieve will work. Pass the flour, baking soda, and salt through it into a bowl, helping the mixture through gently if needed.
The dry ingredients look evenly combined after sifting. Should I stir the chopped chocolate into them now?
Not from the directions provided. They specifically say to sift the flour, baking soda, and salt, then set that mixture aside; they do not yet say to combine it with the chocolate.
So I should leave the sifted mixture in a bowl next to the prepared pans?
Exactly. Set the sifted dry mixture aside and keep the 6 chopped 1 ounce squares of unsweetened chocolate nearby for the later recipe directions.
What should I check before I pause and look for the next part of the recipe?

Confirm that the oven is at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), 2 floured 9 inch pans are ready, and the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt are set aside. The supplied instructions end there, so baking and serving details will need the remaining recipe directions.
Let's make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. I want to keep the ingredients and steps organized.
Certainly. We'll organize the ingredients first and then follow the cooking cues in order.
Before I handle the next part of Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Begin the prep station with 2 tablespoons minced garlic; 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes. Leave these items easy to identify so the next addition stays unambiguous.
As I continue with Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, how do I tell that this part is settled?
The next ingredients to stage are 1 tablespoon dried basil; 1 cube vegetable bouillon. Leave these items easy to identify so the next addition stays unambiguous.
For the current stage of Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, what should I prepare or inspect?
Place squash halves cut side down on the baking sheet. Pause afterward to make sure the stage looks even.
With Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style in front of me, what belongs within reach now?
Bake squash 35 minutes in the preheated oven, or until a knife can be easily inserted. While this happens, watch the texture closely.
Before I handle the next part of Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, what belongs within reach now?
Remove from oven, and cool. At that point, use the finished appearance as the checkpoint.
For the current stage of Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, what should I pay attention to before proceeding?
Meanwhile, spray a non-stick saucepan with cooking spray. At that stage leave the result undisturbed rather than inventing a new finish.
With Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style in front of me, which practical detail matters next?
No further handling is needed at this stage; keep the prepared items together and continue in the recipe's order.
Before I start the Crawfish Chowder, could you give me two ways to handle a little chili at the end? I just want to consider them, not pick one yet.
Sure. The first way is to add the chili late as a streak over only part of the dish. The second is to stir the chili evenly through the whole dish. Either can stay on the table for now.
Please keep those two Crawfish Chowder ideas in that same order in my notes. I'll decide after I see what feels right.
I'll keep them as two open possibilities, with the partial late streak listed before the evenly mixed-in chili.
I have a large skillet ready. What should I put beside the stove before I start?
Set out 1/4 cup butter and 1/2 bunch chopped green onions first. Have a spoon or spatula ready for sautéing and a bowl or plate nearby for the onions.
The first butter and the onions are measured. What else should be within reach?
Keep the remaining 1/2 cup butter and 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned, close by, along with a second bowl or plate for the crawfish after they cook.
Everything is arranged. How should I heat the skillet?
Put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter.
The butter has melted without browning. What am I looking for with the green onions?
Add the chopped green onions and sauté them in the butter until they are tender. Keep the heat at medium so they soften rather than scorch.
The onions are soft and tender now. Should they stay in the skillet?
Remove the tender green onions from the pan and set them aside.
The skillet is empty again, and the onions are waiting on the side. What goes in next?
In that same skillet, melt the remaining 1/2 cup butter. Then add the 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned.
Once the crawfish are in the butter, how long should I sauté them?
Sauté the crawfish for 5 minutes, then set them aside as well.
The crawfish are set aside. I'm going to leave the chili question open until I see the dish rather than choose either approach now.
That keeps both options available: the first remains a late chili streak over only part of the dish, and the second remains chili stirred evenly throughout the whole dish.
I'm making Empanadas tomorrow. What should I set out for the dough?

Gather 1/2 cup softened butter, 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese, and 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour. Keep 1 cup fruit preserves nearby as well. A mixing bowl, spoon or mixer, and foil or cling wrap will be useful.
The butter is soft and the cream cheese is out. Should I prepare anything else before mixing?
Make sure you have space in the refrigerator for the wrapped dough. You do not need to heat anything for the dough preparation.
I have the butter and cream cheese in my bowl. What am I looking for as I mix them?
Cream them together until they are smoothly blended. Scrape down the bowl if needed so there are no obvious separate streaks of butter or cream cheese.
The mixture looks smooth. When does the flour go in?
Beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour. Stop once it has been worked into the cream cheese mixture and forms the dough.
The flour is incorporated and the dough is holding together. How should I store it?
Shape the dough into a smooth ball, then wrap it in foil or cling wrap. Refrigerate it overnight; it can stay refrigerated for up to 1 week.
I plan to use it tomorrow. Should the fruit preserves go into the refrigerator too?
Have the 1 cup fruit preserves ready for when you use the dough. The directions provided list the preserves but do not give further filling or baking details.
Tomorrow, how long before using the chilled dough should I take it out?
At baking time, remove the dough from the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it so it can sit briefly before you work with it.
Is there another baking temperature or time I should follow after that?
No temperature or baking duration is included in the supplied directions. The last stated preparation instruction is to let the refrigerated dough stand for 30 minutes before using.
I have Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats in mind and the potatoes are already baked. What should I get ready before I start assembling them?

Set out 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, and 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. Sliced green onions can be ready too if you want the optional garnish. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
What tools will make the scooping and filling less messy?
Use a baking sheet or oven-safe dish for the potato pieces, a spoon for scooping, and a small spoon or brush to spread the Ranch inside the skins. Keep the shredded Cheddar nearby for the topping.
The potato quarters are on the tray. Should I remove all of the potato from each skin?

Scoop the potato out of the skins while keeping the skins intact enough to hold the filling. Leave the skins on the tray, since you will coat their insides with Ranch and then put the scooped potato back in.
How much Ranch should go into the skins?
Use the full 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing to coat the inside of the potato skins. Spread it around the interior rather than letting it pool in one spot.
The Ranch is spread inside the skins. What goes back in first?
Return the scooped potato to the Ranch-coated skins, dividing it among the quarters so each one is filled.
They are filled again. When do I add the Cheddar?
Sprinkle the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese over the filled potato boats. Try to cover the potato evenly so each piece gets some cheese.
The oven is at 375 degrees F and the cheese is on. The recipe does not give a baking time—what should I watch for?

Put the topped boats in the oven and watch for the Cheddar to melt and the potatoes to heat through. Since no exact baking duration is given, use the melted, hot cheese as the cue rather than relying on a set number of minutes.
The cheese has melted and the edges of the skins look hot and crisp. Are they ready to serve?
Yes. Let them sit briefly so they are easier to handle, then add sliced green onions if you want. Serve the Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats while the cheese is still melted.
I'm making Curried Winter Squash. Can you guide me from getting the ingredients out through serving?

Absolutely. Gather a medium microwave-safe bowl, a spoon or spatula, and the cooked squash. You'll need 3 cups mashed winter squash, 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
My squash is already cooked and mashed. Should I measure everything before I start?
Yes. Measure the curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup first so they are ready to add to the bowl with the squash.
Everything is measured. What goes into the bowl?
Put the 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash in the medium bowl. Add the 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
Should I stir before microwaving, even if the butter is still firm?
Stir the ingredients together as well as you can. The butter can be in small pieces; it will melt as the squash heats.
The bowl is mixed and ready. How long does it need?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, what should I look for before serving?
The squash should be hot throughout and the butter or margarine should be melted into the mixture. Give it a careful stir so the curry and maple syrup are evenly distributed.
It is hot, but the center seems a little cooler than the edges.
Stir from the edges into the center, then continue heating only until the center is hot as well. Use the original about-5-minute timing as a guide rather than overheating it.
It is evenly hot now. Is there anything to add on top?
If you have coconut and would like it, sprinkle some over the finished squash. It is optional.
I'll leave the coconut off. Is it ready to plate?
Yes. Spoon the Curried Winter Squash into a serving dish or onto plates and serve while it is hot.
I'm putting together Baked French Toast 2 tonight. What pan and bread prep should I start with?
Butter a 9x13 inch baking dish. Slice the 1 pound loaf of French bread diagonally into 1 inch slices, then arrange the slices across the bottom of the dish.
The bread is in the buttered dish. What should I measure for the custard?
Set out 8 eggs, 2 cups milk, and 1 1/2 cups half-and-half cream. You'll also need 2 teaspoons vanilla extract and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Everything is measured. Should I mix the custard before I touch the bread again?
Yes. In a large bowl, beat the eggs with the milk, half-and-half, vanilla, and cinnamon until the mixture is evenly combined.
The egg mixture is smooth, and the bread slices are still arranged in one layer. How do I add it?
Pour the custard over the bread slices, aiming to moisten the whole layer. Cover the dish and refrigerate it overnight so the bread can absorb the mixture.
Before it goes into the refrigerator, should I press the bread down?
A gentle press is fine if a few slices are floating, but do not mash them. The custard should be distributed over the bread and the dish should be covered securely.
It has chilled overnight. What temperature should I use in the morning?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Use the recipe's doneness cue as you bake rather than guessing from the clock.
I'd like the topping ready near serving time. What do I do with the sauce ingredients?
In a small saucepan, combine the butter, brown sugar, and corn syrup. Heat them until the mixture is bubbling.
The sauce is bubbling and the French toast is nearly ready. What should I check before I bring it to the table?
Make sure the baked custard is set and the bread is heated through, then check that the sauce is smooth and bubbling. Spoon or pour the warm sauce over the French toast when serving.
I'm making Aunt Mamies today. Before I start, can you help me organize the ingredients and tools?

Set out 1 (8 ounce) package softened cream cheese, 1/2 cup softened butter, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 1/3 cup milk, and 1/2 pound ground walnuts. You'll also want a mixing bowl, a cover for chilling the dough, a saucepan, and a spoon for stirring.
The ingredient list says butter, but one direction says margarine. Which should I use?
Use the 1/2 cup softened butter listed with the ingredients. Beat it with the softened cream cheese until the mixture is smooth and well blended, without obvious lumps of either ingredient.
The cream cheese and butter are blended. Should the flour go in all at once?
Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour and mix until it forms a cohesive dough. Shape the dough into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours.
While the dough chills, can I get the filling ingredients ready?
Yes. Measure the 1 cup white sugar and 1/3 cup milk for the saucepan, and keep the 1/2 pound ground walnuts nearby for after the sugar mixture is cooked.
The dough has chilled for 2 hours and feels firm. What do I do with the sugar and milk?
Put the sugar and milk in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir occasionally as it heats, continuing until the milk boils and the sugar has dissolved.
How can I tell whether the sugar has really dissolved before I move on?
The liquid should no longer feel or look grainy from undissolved sugar, and it should have reached a boil. Stir across the bottom and sides of the pan so no sugar is left sitting there.
It has boiled, and the mixture looks smooth. Are the walnuts next?
Yes—add the ground walnuts to the hot sugar-and-milk mixture. Stir them in, then remove the saucepan from the heat.
It is off the heat now. How cool should the walnut mixture be before I use it?

Let it cool until it reaches a spreading consistency: thick enough to stay where you spread it, but still soft enough to spread without tearing the chilled dough. The directions provided end at that point, so use the cooled filling with the remaining shaping or assembly directions from your recipe.
I'm making Garden Potato Salad. The potatoes are cooked, peeled, and ready to cube. What should I gather before I start mixing?
Set out a large bowl, 6 large cooked potatoes, 4 hard-cooked eggs, 2 celery ribs, and 6 green onions with their tops. Cube the potatoes and slice the eggs, celery, and onions before combining them.
My potatoes are cubed and the vegetables are sliced. Should the eggs go into the bowl now or wait for the dressing?
Add the sliced hard-cooked eggs to the large bowl with the potatoes, celery, and green onions. The recipe also calls for radishes, salt, and pepper in that bowl, then has you set the mixture aside.
I see the radishes, salt, and pepper mentioned in the directions, but their amounts aren't in my ingredient note. What do I do with that?

Use the amounts given on your full recipe card if you have them. The directions clearly place the radishes, salt, and pepper with the potato mixture, but the ingredient note you have does not specify quantities for them.
The bowl is combined and set aside. What needs to be ready at the stove for the dressing?
Bring out a saucepan and the dressing ingredients named in the recipe: eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt. Combine them in the saucepan before turning on the heat.
The dressing ingredients are in the saucepan. What heat should I use?
Cook the dressing over medium heat, stirring as it cooks. Keep it moving so you can notice when it thickens.
How thick should the dressing become before I stop cooking it?
Stop when it has thickened. The recipe does not give a time, so use the change in texture rather than a clock and continue stirring over medium heat until you reach that point.
The dressing has thickened and I took the saucepan off the heat. Can I mix it into the potatoes right away?
Cool the dressing before proceeding; "Cool" is the recipe's final instruction. Once it is cooled, handle the potato mixture gently so the cubed potatoes and sliced eggs stay intact.
The dressing is cool and the salad is assembled. Is there anything to check before serving?

Check that the potato mixture is evenly coated and that the sliced eggs, celery, green onions, and any radishes are distributed through the salad. Taste for salt and pepper if those were added, then serve it cooled.
Let's work through Badische Schupfnudeln Potato Noodles today. Where should I begin?

Yes. Start by gathering 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley. You will also need a large pot, a peeler, a lightly floured work surface, a rolling pin, and a bowl.
Should I measure the flour before I start boiling the potatoes?
Measure the full 1/2 cup now so it is ready later. If it helps with measuring, you can fill a 1/4-cup measure twice; keep the flour nearby for the work surface and the potato mixture.
My pot of water is boiling. Do the potatoes go in peeled or unpeeled?
Put the potatoes in whole, with their skins on, and boil them for 25 to 30 minutes. Keep enough water in the pot to cover them as they cook.
How can I tell whether the potatoes have cooked long enough?
At the end of the 25 to 30 minutes, a fork or knife should slide into a potato with little resistance. Drain the pot and discard the water once they are tender.
The potatoes are drained but still very hot. What should I prepare while they cool?

Set out the flour, egg, and chopped parsley, and dust a clean work surface lightly with flour. Let the potatoes cool only until you can handle them safely; they are easier to work with while still warm.
They are cool enough to touch. Should I peel them directly over the floured counter?
Peel the potatoes, then place them on the lightly floured surface. Remove all of the skin before working on the potato flesh.
I have peeled them. What is the right way to mash them without making them gummy?
Use the rolling pin to mash the potatoes across the floured surface. Press and roll until the potato is broken down into an even, mostly smooth layer rather than large chunks.
There are a few small lumps left. Should I keep rolling?
Keep mashing until the lumps are small enough that the potatoes look fairly uniform. Avoid repeatedly stirring or overworking them; the supplied instructions stop after the potatoes are mashed.
I have a smooth mashed potato layer now. When do the flour, egg, and parsley get added?

The ingredient list includes the 1/2 cup flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, but the instructions provided do not state how to combine, shape, cook, or serve the noodles after mashing. Check the remaining recipe directions before adding them so you do not guess at the next stage.
Golden Cheese Yeast Bread is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track?

Set a large mixing bowl near the mixer and measure the dry ingredients before you begin. You'll use 6 cups all-purpose flour total, but start with 3 cups; also have 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese, 3 tablespoons sugar, 2 (.25 ounce) packages active dry yeast, and 2 teaspoons salt ready.
I have the dry ingredients out. Should the milk and egg be ready before I combine them?
Yes. Keep 2 cups warm milk and an egg beside the bowl. The milk should be warm, not hot, so it is ready to add as soon as the dry mixture is combined.
The bowl has 3 cups of flour, the Cheddar, sugar, yeast, and salt. Is that the right starting mixture?
That is right. Mix those ingredients together in the large bowl so the cheese, yeast, sugar, and salt are distributed through the flour.
Everything looks evenly mixed. How should I add the milk and egg?
Add the warm milk and egg, then beat on low speed until the mixture is smooth. Scrape down the bowl if dry flour is clinging to the sides.
It is smooth but still more like a thick batter than dough. Do I add all of the remaining flour?
Add the remaining flour gradually, stirring only until you have a soft dough. You may not need every bit of the flour; stop when the dough holds together and is soft rather than wet and pourable.
The dough is gathered into a soft ball and feels slightly tacky. What should I do on the counter?

Turn it onto a lightly floured surface and knead until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Use only enough flour on the surface to keep it manageable, since too much can make the bread heavy.
After kneading, the surface is smoother and the dough springs back a little when pressed. Is it ready to rise?
Yes. Put it in a greased bowl, turning it once so the top is greased as well. Cover the bowl and leave it in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
While it rises, what should I check before moving on to the rest of the recipe?

Look for a clear doubling in volume and a puffy, airy feel rather than relying on the clock alone. Once it has risen, follow the remaining shaping and baking directions from your recipe; after baking, check that the bread has a good texture and is ready to serve.
I'm making Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I mix anything?
Yes. Put out a large bowl, plus 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar for the creaming stage.
I have those in front of me. Which wet ingredients do I need alongside them?
Measure 1/2 cup molasses and separate 1 egg yolk. Those get stirred in after the margarine and sugar are smooth.
What dry ingredients should I gather before my hands get sticky?
Have the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg ready to combine. The recipe calls for that dry mixture to be blended into the molasses mixture.
My margarine and sugar are in the large bowl. What should the creamed mixture look like?
Cream them together until the mixture looks smooth, without visible separate bits of margarine or dry sugar.
It looks smooth now. Can I add the molasses and yolk together?
Yes. Stir in the 1/2 cup molasses and the egg yolk until they are evenly incorporated.
The mixture is dark and glossy. Should I dump in all the dry ingredients at once?
Combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg, then blend that mixture into the molasses base until the dough is smooth.
How do I know when the dough is ready for the refrigerator?
Once the dry ingredients are blended in and the dough is smooth, cover the bowl and chill it for at least one hour.
The bowl is covered. Is there anything else in these directions I should do before chilling?
No additional shaping, baking, or serving directions are included here. Chill the covered dough for at least one hour before moving on to any later instructions you have.
I'm ready to cook Garden Potato Salad. What should be ready before I begin? I have a large bowl and a saucepan ready, and I want to organize the prep before I begin.

You'll use the large bowl for the salad and the saucepan for the dressing. Set out the cooked potatoes, eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, pepper, and the dressing ingredients: eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt.
I have 6 large potatoes cooked, peeled, and cubed, plus 4 hard-cooked eggs sliced. What produce should I finish slicing?
Slice 2 celery ribs, 6 green onions with their tops, and 6 radishes. Have 1 teaspoon salt and pepper ready as well.
The potatoes and sliced vegetables are in front of me. Should the salad ingredients go into the bowl before I make the dressing?
Yes. Put the potatoes, sliced eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper in the large bowl. Combine them gently and set the bowl aside while you prepare the dressing.
The potato mixture is ready. What goes into the saucepan?
In the saucepan, combine the eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt for the dressing before turning on the heat.
Everything is mixed in the saucepan. How should I cook it?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring continuously, until the dressing thickens. Keep the spoon moving along the bottom and sides so it heats evenly.
It is starting to look thicker and less runny. Is that the point to take it off the burner?
Once it has clearly thickened, remove the saucepan from the heat. Let the dressing cool before it goes into the potato salad.
The dressing has cooled. I see mayonnaise mentioned with the finishing steps—where does that fit?
Stir the mayonnaise into the cooled dressing and mix well. Then pour the dressing over the potato mixture.
The dressing is over the potatoes. What is the best way to finish without breaking up the cubes and egg slices?
Toss gently until the potatoes and vegetables are coated. Before serving, check that the dressing is evenly distributed and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper only if needed.
Chipotle Mayo Relish is on deck today. What should I do first?
Absolutely. You'll blend the mayonnaise with chipotle, fold in the onion and relish, then chill it until you're ready to serve.
What ingredients should I set out, and do I need any special equipment?

Gather 1 cup light mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce that have been seeded and minced, 1/4 cup chopped green onion, and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish. You'll need a food processor, a spoon or spatula, and a serving bowl.
The chipotles are seeded and minced. Should the adobo sauce stay nearby?
Yes. Process the light mayonnaise and minced chipotles together until the mixture is evenly blended. Keep the adobo sauce nearby in case you want a little more smoky heat.
It's smooth and pale orange, with tiny chipotle flecks. How much extra sauce can I add?
Taste it if you like, then add extra adobo sauce only if you want more heat. About 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount to add, and you can process briefly again so it is fully incorporated.
The heat level works for me. Do the green onion and pickle relish go into the processor too?
Transfer the chipotle mayo to your serving bowl instead. Stir in the 1/4 cup chopped green onion and the 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish by hand, so those pieces remain distinct.
I've folded them in. What texture should I be looking for?

It should be creamy and spreadable, with visible bits of green onion and sweet relish distributed throughout. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl once or twice to make sure there are no plain pockets of mayonnaise.
It looks evenly mixed. Can I serve it right away?
You can, but it is best to chill it until serving. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it so the flavors settle and the relish firms up slightly.
It has chilled, and I'm about to put it on the table. Anything to check?
Give the Chipotle Mayo Relish a final stir, then check that it is creamy rather than watery and that the chipotle flavor suits you. Spoon it into a clean serving bowl and serve it chilled.
I'm making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf tonight. Can you help me get the oven and pan work underway?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Put a skillet, slotted spoon, paper towels, and a heat-safe container or place for the cooked bacon near the stove.
What should I chop and measure while the oven heats?

Chop 1 small white onion and 5 button mushrooms. Measure 12 ounces of raw bacon and have 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef ready. If your recipe card includes the binder items, measure 1 egg and 1/4 cup evaporated milk as well.
The bacon is in a cold skillet. What heat should I use?
Use medium heat and let the bacon cook until the pieces are browned. Stir or turn them occasionally so they color evenly without scorching.
Some pieces are crisp and brown, while a few are still pale at the fatty edges. Should I take anything out yet?
Wait until the batch is generally browned, then lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon and drain it on the paper towels. Leaving the rendered fat in the skillet for the moment is fine.
The bacon is draining. How much grease stays in the pan?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of bacon grease. That remaining amount is enough for cooking the chopped onion and mushrooms.
I've kept the tablespoon of grease. What should the vegetables look like before I stop cooking them?
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook them until soft. The onion should lose its raw-looking firmness, and the mushrooms should soften rather than remain chunky and rigid.
The mushrooms have released moisture and the onion is soft. I'm worried about a soggy loaf—what should I do before mixing?

Take the skillet off the heat and let the vegetables cool enough that they will not warm the raw beef immediately. Their moisture should be cooked down somewhat, but they do not need to be browned hard.
I'm ready to combine everything. What is the gentlest way to handle the 1 1/2 pounds of beef?

Put the extra-lean ground beef in a large bowl with the cooled bacon, onion, and mushrooms, plus the 1 egg and 1/4 cup evaporated milk if those are listed on your card. Mix only until the ingredients are distributed; overworking the meat can make the loaf dense.
Before it goes into the oven, what should I check?

Make sure the mixture is evenly combined without pockets of unmixed beef or vegetables, then shape it in its pan and bake in the preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) oven. After baking, let the loaf settle briefly before slicing so it holds together cleanly.
Armadillo Eggs is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top?
Absolutely. Start by preheating the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), then lightly grease a medium baking sheet so it is ready when you need it.
While the oven heats, what ingredients should I put on the counter?
Gather 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package shredded Cheddar cheese.
I have the peppers washed and a small knife ready. How should I open them?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno. Make the opening large enough to reach the inside without cutting the pepper completely in half.
Should I remove only the seeds, or the pale inside part too?
Remove and discard both the seeds and the pulp from each pepper. Clear the cavity thoroughly, then set the cleaned peppers aside on a clean plate or tray.
A few peppers are much larger than the others. Is that a problem at this stage?
That is fine for the prep. Just make sure every jalapeno has a slit and has been cleared of seeds and pulp; the different sizes do not change those steps.
All 24 peppers are slit and cleaned. What should I check before I move on?
Check that the baking sheet is lightly greased, the oven is holding at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), and the sausage, baking mix, and shredded Cheddar are measured and within reach.
The peppers are ready, and I have the 1 pound of sausage, 2 cups of baking mix, and the 16 ounce package of Cheddar set out. Do I need to do anything else to the peppers?

Based on the supplied instructions, the pepper preparation is complete once the slits are cut and the seeds and pulp have been discarded. Keep the peppers on the prepared baking sheet or another clean surface while you continue with the remaining recipe directions.
Before I start assembling, can you give me a quick recap of what I have completed?

You have preheated the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), lightly greased a medium baking sheet, cut a slit in each of the 24 jalapenos, and removed and discarded their seeds and pulp. Your sausage, baking mix, and shredded Cheddar are also ready for the next part.
I'm making Argentine Chimichurri Bread in my bread machine. Can you help me set up before I start?

Set out the bread-machine pan and the ingredients listed for the loaf: 1 cup water, 1 1/2 tablespoons white wine vinegar, 3 tablespoons olive oil, and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper. Check your machine manual for the order it recommends for adding ingredients.
I only have a 3/4-cup measure handy. What is the easiest way to portion the water?
Use the 3/4-cup measure once, then add 1/4 cup more to make the required 1 cup of water.
The water, vinegar, oil, and cayenne are measured. Should I put them straight into the pan?
Yes—add everything to the bread-machine pan in the sequence specified by your manufacturer. That order matters more than choosing a universal liquid-first or dry-first approach.
The pan is in the machine now. Which setting should I use?
Choose the Basic or White cycle, then press Start.
It has started mixing. Is there anything useful to check without interrupting it?

Let the machine run its programmed cycle. If your model allows a quick look through the lid without stopping it, confirm that the ingredients are being incorporated, but avoid changing the cycle or adding anything not called for.
The loaf is partway through the cycle and the machine is doing the work. When should I intervene?
There is no additional recipe step during the cycle. Leave the pan in place and let the Basic or White program continue through baking.
The cycle is nearly done. How can I tell when it is time to take the bread out?
Wait until the selected cycle has completed, then use oven mitts to remove the hot pan. Turn the loaf out carefully rather than leaving it to steam in the pan for too long.
Once it is out of the pan, how should I serve it?

Let the Argentine Chimichurri Bread cool enough to slice cleanly, then cut and serve it while it is still pleasantly warm. Wipe out the pan after it has cooled before washing it according to the manufacturer's directions.
I'm making Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker tonight. What size cooker should I use, and what should I gather?

Use a 5-qt. slow cooker. Gather 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2-inch cubes, 1 medium chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, a 14.5-ounce can of chicken broth, and the sausage.
My cabbage is shredded, but I still need to cut the potatoes. How small should the cubes be?
Cut the 3 medium potatoes into roughly 1/2-inch cubes so they can become tender during the long low cook.
The potatoes and onion are ready. Do the vegetables all go into the cooker before the liquid?
Yes. Put the shredded cabbage, cubed potatoes, and chopped onion into the slow cooker. Add the 1 3/4 teaspoons salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper, then combine them in the cooker.
It looks very full already. Should I try to pack the cabbage down?
It is expected to be full at this point. You can settle the cabbage gently, but do not worry if it reaches near the top; it will cook down.
Where does the chicken broth go?
Pour the full 14.5-ounce can of chicken broth over the cabbage and vegetables.
The broth is in, and the cabbage is still piled high. When should I add the kielbasa?
Lay the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. Keeping it on top matches the recipe, even though the cooker is full.
It's covered now. What setting and timing should I use?
Cook it covered on low for 8 to 9 hours.
For Cabbage Kielbasa Supper, when I check near the end, what tells me it is ready to serve?
The potatoes and cabbage should be tender, and the sausage should be heated through. If the vegetables are still firm, continue cooking until they are tender before serving.
I'm making Carrot and Coriander Soup II. I've got the carrots, onion, broth, and cilantro ready—how should I prep the station?
Cut 4 large carrots into 1 inch pieces and chop 1/4 large onion. Measure 1 quart vegetable broth and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, then have a large saucepan ready.
Should the cilantro wait until later, or can it go in with the vegetables?
It goes in at the beginning. Place the carrots, onion, vegetable broth, and cilantro together in the large saucepan.
Everything is in the saucepan. What heat and timing should I use?
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
How can I tell when the carrots are ready before I blend the soup?
Check that the carrot pieces are tender when pierced. Once they are, remove the saucepan from the heat and let the soup cool slightly.
It has cooled a little. Is a blender required, or can I use my food processor?
Either works. Transfer the soup to a blender or food processor and puree it until smooth, taking care with the still-warm mixture.
What texture should I look for while pureeing?
Keep blending until the soup is smooth, with the carrot pieces and cilantro fully incorporated rather than remaining chunky.
Once it is smooth, is there another cooking step in this recipe?
No further cooking step is specified. After pureeing, check that the texture is smooth and the soup is ready to serve.
Can you recap the quantities before I finish cleaning up?
You used 4 large carrots cut into 1 inch pieces, 1/4 large onion, 1 quart vegetable broth, and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro.
I'm making a Cookie Bowl. I have a 9x5 inch loaf pan—can I use that as the mold?
Yes. Turn the 9x5 inch loaf pan upside down, then cover its outside with foil. Smooth the foil over the shape so it stays in place.
Should I prepare the oven before I handle the dry ingredients?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is ready when your pan and mixture are prepared.
I'm measuring the dry ingredients now. What amounts do I need?
Measure 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds.
The foil-covered loaf pan is ready. Where does it go?
Set the upside-down, foil-covered pan onto a cookie sheet. The cookie sheet will support the mold while it is in the oven.
I have the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds in a bowl. Do I combine them all at once?
Yes. Stir together the flour, cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds until the cocoa and salt are evenly distributed through the flour. Then set the mixture aside.
What should the dry mixture look like before I stop stirring?
It should look evenly brown from the cocoa, without visible pockets of salt or pale streaks of flour. The sliced almonds should be spread throughout rather than clumped in one spot.
The oven is heating, and the cookie sheet with the covered pan is ready. Is there anything I should check on the foil?
Check that the foil covers the outside of the inverted pan completely and lies fairly smooth against it. Make sure the pan is stable on the cookie sheet before it goes into the oven.
So at this point, the dry ingredients are mixed and set aside, and the mold is on the cookie sheet?

Exactly. You should have the oven at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), the upside-down foil-covered 9x5 inch loaf pan on a cookie sheet, and the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds stirred together and set aside.
I'm making Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. What should I gather before I start?

Set out 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini, and 1 teaspoon dried basil. Have a soup pot, knife, cutting board, and spoon ready too.
The zucchini is whole and the other ingredients are measured. Do I make the soup base before opening the tortellini?
Yes. Prepare the Fast Chicken Soup Base in your soup pot according to its directions. You can dice the zucchini while the base is cooking.
How small should I cut the zucchini for the soup?
Dice the 2 medium zucchini into bite-size pieces so they can become tender in the same cooking time as the tortellini.
The chicken soup base is ready in the pot. What am I looking for before I add the vegetables and pasta?
Bring the base to a simmer: you should see steady small bubbles across the surface, rather than a hard rolling boil.
It is gently simmering now, and I have the can open and the zucchini diced. What goes in?
Stir in the 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with its juices, the diced zucchini, and 1 teaspoon dried basil.
The tortellini floated up after I stirred. Should the pot stay at a simmer?
Yes, keep it at a gentle simmer. Cook for 10–20 minutes, stirring occasionally so the tortellini does not settle on the bottom.
What should I check near the short end of that cooking time?
Taste a tortellini and a piece of zucchini. Continue simmering only until both are tender and the tomatoes are hot throughout.
Everything is tender. I have fresh parsley chopped—when should that be added?
Before taking the soup off the heat, stir in 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley. Give the soup a final stir, then serve while the tortellini are tender.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies. I have a microwave-safe bowl and my mixer out; what ingredients should I measure first?

Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips, 1 cup softened butter (no substitutes), 1/2 cup sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Also have the egg, milk, and vanilla called for in the directions ready to add later.
The butter is soft, and I've measured the sugars and chips. Should I melt the chips before I start mixing?
Yes. Melt the 1 cup of butterscotch chips in the microwave, then let them cool for 10 minutes. Use a bowl large enough to stir them smooth, and avoid adding them while they are still hot.
The chips are melted and cooling. What can I do with the mixer while I wait?
Cream the softened 1 cup butter with the 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Mix until the sugars are evenly worked into the butter and the mixture looks lighter and smooth.
My butter-and-sugar mixture is creamy, and the chips have had their 10 minutes. What goes in next?
Add the egg, milk, and vanilla, then mix well. Once those are incorporated, beat in the cooled melted butterscotch chips.
The melted chips are smooth but still a little warm to the touch. Is that cool enough to use?
They should be cooled rather than hot before they go into the bowl. If the bowl feels noticeably warm, give the chips a little longer so they do not heat the butter mixture when you beat them in.
I've beaten in the chips and the mixture is a uniform butterscotch color. Should I keep mixing for a long time?
Mix only until the melted chips are fully blended through and there are no streaks. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl once if needed, then stop rather than overworking the mixture.
I'm ready to continue, but the directions I have end after beating in the melted chips. Is there a baking temperature or time listed?

The directions provided stop after the melted chips are beaten in, so they do not give a baking temperature, baking time, shaping method, or a doneness cue. Check the full recipe card or its original source before portioning or baking the dough.
While I look that up, what should I clean so the kitchen stays manageable?

Wash the bowl or utensil used for melting the chips before the residue sets, wipe any splatters from the microwave, and keep the mixing bowl covered if you need to pause. Leave the mixer attachment ready only if you expect to resume soon.
I'm starting Banana Bran Muffins. The oven is cold and the muffin pan is still in the cupboard—what should I handle before mixing?
Heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), then grease the muffin pan or line it with paper muffin liners.
While it heats, which ingredients should I measure and set near the mixing bowl?
Set out 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3 mashed bananas, and 1/4 cup milk. Have 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 2 eggs ready as well.
The butter is soft, and I have a large bowl and mixer ready. What should the butter and sugar look like before I add anything else?
Cream the butter and brown sugar together until the mixture looks light and fluffy, with no obvious lumps of butter.
It is pale and fluffy now. Can the bananas, milk, vanilla, and eggs go in together?
Yes. Add the mashed bananas, milk, vanilla, and eggs, then mix until the wet mixture is evenly combined.
The batter looks loose and banana-speckled. I have the flour, bran, baking powder, soda, and salt measured beside it.
Stir in the flour, bran, baking powder, soda, and salt. Mix only until moistened; stop once you no longer see dry streaks rather than beating the batter smooth.
There are no dry patches left, though the batter is still a little lumpy. Should I keep stirring?
No—those small lumps are fine. Overmixing at this point can make the muffins less tender.
I also have the walnuts ready. When do they belong in the batter?
Stir in the walnuts gently, using just enough folds to distribute them through the batter.
The walnuts are spread through evenly, and the prepared muffin pan is waiting. Is there anything else to check in the bowl?
Make sure the batter is uniformly moistened and the walnuts are dispersed, then follow the remaining recipe directions for portioning and baking.
I'm about to work on Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts. Can you keep the preparation in a sensible order?
Yes. We'll work from preparation into cooking and pause at the useful visual cues.
For the current stage of Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Measure this first group: 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice; 2 tablespoons orange flower water. Leave these items in its own part of the counter until the recipe calls for it.
At this point in Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts, which cue should guide the next move?
Have 2 cups all-purpose flour; 2 tablespoons vegetable oil beside the first group, without combining anything early.
With Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts in front of me, which practical detail matters next?
Let the almonds soak in water for about 5 minutes, then drain and peel. Take a moment afterward and check the immediate result.
With Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts in front of me, what belongs within reach now?
Spread the almonds on baking sheets, and bake at 200 degrees F(95 degrees C) until completely dry and toasted. During this part, keep the heat and movement steady.
At this point in Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts, what should I prepare or inspect?
This takes several hours, and needs to be prepared ahead. Before moving on, make sure the food has reached the described state.
With Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts in front of me, what should I prepare or inspect?
Be careful not to burn the nuts, as this will give a bitter taste to the filling. Once it is complete, keep the pieces or mixture as arranged until the following instruction.
Before I handle the next part of Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts, what should I pay attention to before proceeding?
The food and work area are ready to advance. Move into the following written instruction when ready.
I'm ready to make the German Sweet Chocolate Pie. What should I set out before I start?

Set out 1 (4 ounce) bar German sweet chocolate, chopped; 1/3 cup milk; 4 ounces softened cream cheese; and 2 tablespoons white sugar. You'll also need a large microwave-safe bowl, a wire whisk, and a spatula.
I also have the topping and crust ready. Is there anything specific I should check?
Make sure the 1 (12 ounce) container of frozen whipped topping is thawed, and have a 1 (9 inch) prepared graham cracker crust nearby. Measure 2 tablespoons of the milk separately for the chocolate.
The chocolate is chopped and the ingredients are measured. What happens in the microwave?
Put the chopped chocolate in the large microwave-safe bowl with the 2 tablespoons of milk. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chocolate is almost melted.
It's nearly melted, with a few soft pieces left. Should I heat it again?
No extra heating is needed if it is almost melted. Stir it until smooth, then add the softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk.
How should I combine that mixture?
Beat everything together with a wire whisk until the chocolate, cream cheese, sugar, and milk are blended. Once the mixture is even, refrigerate it for 10 minutes.
The 10 minutes are up. The filling is cool now—what is the next texture check?
Fold in 3 1/2 cups of the thawed whipped topping gently with a spatula. Stop when no streaks remain so the filling stays light.
The filling looks uniform. Do I put it straight into the crust?
Yes. Spoon the filling into the prepared 9 inch graham cracker crust and smooth the top without pressing it down.
How long should the assembled pie chill before serving?
Freeze the pie for 4 hours. After that, check that the center is set and the slices hold their shape before serving.
I'm making Baked Aloha Chicken. I have chicken legs, an ovenproof glass baking dish, and a mixing bowl. What should I measure before I begin?

Measure 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup light corn syrup, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon salt. Also have the ginger, corn oil, and crushed pineapple with its liquid ready, since they go into the sauce.
Should I heat the oven while I make the sauce?
Yes—preheat it to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is ready when the chicken is assembled.
The lemon juice, syrup, soy sauce, and salt are in my bowl. What consistency am I aiming for before adding the fruit?
Add the ginger and corn oil, then stir everything until the sauce looks smooth and evenly blended, with no visible streaks of syrup or oil.
The sauce is smooth. Do I drain the crushed pineapple?
No. Stir the crushed pineapple in together with its liquid; that liquid is part of the sauce.
My baking dish is clean and the chicken legs are ready. How should I put it together?
Arrange the chicken legs in the ovenproof glass baking dish, then pour the pineapple sauce over the top so the legs are coated.
Some pineapple is sitting on top of the chicken and some has fallen around the sides. Is that okay?
Yes. Spread it roughly evenly over and around the chicken so the sauce is distributed across the dish before it goes into the preheated oven.
I want to make sure I haven't skipped anything. Can you recap the sequence?

Preheat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C); stir together the lemon juice, light corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil until smooth; mix in the crushed pineapple and its liquid; then place the chicken legs in an ovenproof glass baking dish and pour the sauce over them.
Great, the dish is assembled and ready for the oven.
You are set to bake the assembled Baked Aloha Chicken. Keep the dish level when transferring it so the sauce stays around the chicken legs.
I'm about to start Asparagus Sandwiches. Can you talk me through the prep?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (10 ounce) can asparagus tips, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion, 1 pinch seasoning salt, and soft sliced white bread. You'll also want paper towels, a small bowl, a spoon, and a knife for trimming crusts.
The asparagus tips are drained. Should I dry them before I mix the spread?
Yes. Lay the asparagus spears on paper towels and gently blot away excess liquid. Dry spears will keep the bread from becoming soggy.
While they dry, what goes into the bowl?
Stir together the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion, and 1 pinch seasoning salt in the small bowl. Mix until the onion is evenly distributed.
The spread looks smooth, and I have a 1 pound loaf of soft sliced white bread ready. How should I prepare the slices?
Remove the crusts from the bread slices. Spread a thin, even layer of the mayonnaise mixture over each slice; a thick layer can make the rolls slide apart.
I've spread the bread. Are the asparagus tips ready to use if they still feel a little tender?
That is fine—the canned tips should be tender. Just make sure they are no longer visibly wet, then place 1 spear along one edge of each prepared bread slice.
What is the neatest way to roll them without squeezing the filling out?
Roll each slice snugly around the spear, starting at the edge where the asparagus sits. Use light pressure so the roll holds its shape without forcing out the mayonnaise mixture.
A few rolls have uneven ends. Should I trim or cut them before putting them on the tray?
If needed, trim only ragged edges, then cut each roll in half for bite-size sandwiches. Arrange the halves on a serving tray with the seam side down when possible.
They're arranged now, but we won't eat for a little while. How should I hold them?
Cover the tray with plastic wrap and refrigerate the sandwiches until serving. Before bringing them out, check that the rolls are still closed and that no excess moisture has collected on the tray.
I'm about to chop for Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs. Should the oven be heating while I prep?
Yes—preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) before you start cooking. Set out a medium saucepan for the vegetables and a medium bowl for the cooked mixture.
What ingredients should I measure and chop before the pan goes on?
Have 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove garlic, crushed, ready beside the stove. The cooking directions also call for cayenne pepper.
My longer note mentions 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper and 4 ounces softened cream cheese. Should I get those ready too?

If you're using that fuller version, measure the 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper and let the 4 ounces cream cheese soften now. Keep the crabmeat nearby as well, since it is blended in after the mushroom mixture is cooked.
The vegetables are prepped and the oven has reached temperature. How do I start the stovetop part?
Put the medium saucepan over medium heat and heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil. Give it a moment to warm, but it should not be smoking.
The oil is warm and moves easily across the bottom of the pan. Can the vegetables go in?
Add the mushrooms, green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper. Stir so the vegetables are coated with the oil and spread them across the pan.
The mushrooms have started releasing liquid. How long should I keep cooking them?
Cook them for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are tender and the onions have softened. Keep the heat at medium so the garlic does not scorch.
The mushrooms are tender and most of the liquid has cooked away. What should I do before adding the creamy ingredients?
Take the saucepan off the heat and transfer the mushroom mixture to the medium bowl. Letting it sit briefly makes it easier to combine without continued cooking in the hot pan.
The mixture is in the bowl. How will I know it is ready to serve?

Blend in the softened cream cheese and crabmeat until the filling is evenly combined. Check that it is creamy, with tender mushroom pieces throughout, and taste it before serving or using it in the puff preparation.
I have the ingredients for Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches out. Where should I begin?
Certainly. We'll organize the ingredients first and then follow the cooking cues in order.
As I continue with Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, what should I prepare or inspect?
Measure this first group: salt and pepper to taste; 1 French baguette. Hold this set easy to identify until the recipe calls for it.
For the current stage of Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, what belongs within reach now?
Add this second group to the setup: 2 ounces soft goat cheese; 1/4 cup tapenade (olive spread). Hold this set easy to identify until the recipe calls for it.
For the current stage of Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, which cue should guide the next move?
Broil 5 to 10 minutes, until tender and slightly browned. At the end of this move to read the texture.
Before I handle the next part of Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Cut baguette in half lengthwise. Until the cue appears, look for the recipe's intended visual cue.
For the current stage of Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, what should I prepare or inspect?
Spread bottom half with goat cheese, followed by tapenade. Before changing course, look over the result without adding another step.
At this point in Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Layer with eggplant and red pepper, then sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. At that stage leave the result undisturbed as you prepare to continue.
At this point in Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, what should I prepare or inspect?
Yes. Use the recipe's next instruction from here and leave the completed preparation undisturbed.
I'm making Grandmas Gnocchi tonight. I have 6 russet potatoes—what should I get out before I start?
Set out 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, lightly beaten, and 1 tablespoon olive oil. You'll also need salt, a large pot, a colander, a bowl, and a fork for mashing.
The pot is on the stove. Should the potatoes go in before the water boils?
Wait until the large pot of salted water reaches a full boil, then add the potatoes.
How will I know the potatoes have cooked enough?
Cook them for about 15 minutes, until a fork goes in easily but the potatoes are still firm enough to hold together.
While they cook, should I prepare the egg and oil?
Yes. Lightly beat the 1 egg and measure the 1 tablespoon olive oil. Keep the 1 cup flour nearby, but don't mix it in yet.
The potatoes are tender and I've drained them. Are they ready to peel right away?
Let them cool just enough to handle comfortably, then peel them while they are still warm.
They're peeled and in the bowl. Should I use a masher?
Season the potatoes with salt and mash them with a fork. Aim for an even mash without large lumps.
The mash is smooth and still warm. What goes in next?
Stir in the lightly beaten egg and the olive oil until they are evenly incorporated.
I'm ready for the flour. How should the dough feel?
Work in the 1 cup all-purpose flour until you have a soft dough. The directions provided stop there, so use any remaining shaping and cooking directions from your recipe card before serving.
Caramel Shortbread Squares is next on my counter. Help me move through it without losing track of the recipe.
Of course. We'll keep the work area orderly and use the recipe's texture and timing cues as we go.
Before I handle the next part of Caramel Shortbread Squares, which cue should guide the next move?
For the opening setup, have 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour; 1/2 cup butter ready at the work area.
At this point in Caramel Shortbread Squares, what should I pay attention to before proceeding?
Add this second group to the setup: 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar; 2 tablespoons light corn syrup. Keep this group clearly organized before the active cooking begins.
For the current stage of Caramel Shortbread Squares, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Press into 9 inch square baking pan. Before adding anything else and check the immediate result.
For the current stage of Caramel Shortbread Squares, what should I prepare or inspect?
Bake for 20 minutes. As it develops, keep the heat and movement steady.
Before I handle the next part of Caramel Shortbread Squares, which practical detail matters next?
In a 2 quart saucepan, combine 1/2 cup butter, brown sugar, corn syrup, and sweetened condensed milk. Before moving on, look over the result without adding another step.
As I continue with Caramel Shortbread Squares, what should I prepare or inspect?
Bring to a boil. From there keep the pieces or mixture as arranged until the following instruction.
At this point in Caramel Shortbread Squares, how do I tell that this part is settled?
For Caramel Shortbread Squares, use the recipe's next instruction from here and leave the completed preparation undisturbed.
I have the recipe out for Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me set up the counter before I begin?

Set out a large pot, colander, mixing bowl, spoon, and an 11- x 7- x 11/2-inch baking dish. Gather 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack, 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta, and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles; drain the chiles well.
I also see black beans, chili powder, and salt on my recipe card. Should those be ready too?
Yes. Have the black beans ready to spoon onto the rolls, along with 1/2 teaspoon chili powder and 1/8 teaspoon salt for the cheese mixture.
The water is boiling. Do I season it or add oil before the noodles go in?
Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, omitting both salt and fat. When they are tender, drain them well so excess water does not loosen the filling.
The noodles are drained and still warm. What goes into the filling bowl?
Stir together the ricotta, shredded Monterey Jack, drained green chiles, chili powder, and salt until the seasonings and chiles are evenly distributed.
My filling is mixed. Should I cover the whole noodle with it?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle, leaving a small edge clear so the filling is less likely to squeeze out when you roll it.
I have the beans open beside the noodles. How should I add them without making the rolls bulky?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture, dividing them among all 8 noodles rather than piling them in the center.
The beans are on. Which direction should I roll the noodles?
Roll each noodle up jellyroll fashion, beginning at a narrow end. Keep the roll snug enough to hold its shape without pressing out the filling.
I have the baking dish ready. How do the rolls go in?
Coat the 11- x 7- x 11/2-inch baking dish with cooking spray, then place the lasagna rolls in it seam side down so they stay closed.
They are all arranged seam-side down. Is there a useful check before I continue with the rest of my recipe card?

Make sure the rolls are evenly spaced and that no loose seam is facing upward. The steps you have provided do not include baking time or temperature, so use the remaining directions on your recipe card for that part.
I'm making Feta Chicken Salad for lunch. I have 3 cups diced cooked chicken—what should I get on the counter before I begin?

Set out a large serving bowl and a smaller bowl for the dressing. Gather 2 large stalks celery, diced; 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced; 1/2 red onion, diced; mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, dill, salt, and pepper.
The celery, pepper, and onion are chopped. Should the chicken go into the large bowl now?
Yes. Put the 3 cups diced cooked chicken in the serving bowl with the celery and red onion. Keep the bell pepper nearby to fold in with the chicken mixture before dressing it.
The chicken mixture is in the bowl. What goes into the smaller bowl?

Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill in the smaller bowl. Use 6 tablespoons mayonnaise, then mix until the sour cream and mayo look evenly combined and the feta is distributed through the dressing.
The dressing is creamy, with small feta crumbles still visible. Is that the texture I want?
That sounds right. The feta does not need to dissolve; you just want the dressing mixed well enough that each scoop has some feta and dill.
I've added the bell pepper to the chicken bowl. Should I pour in all of the dressing?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and fold gently until the chicken, celery, onion, and pepper are coated. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl once or twice so there are no dry pockets.
It looks a little thick while I'm folding. Should I add anything?
No extra ingredient is needed. Continue folding just until the dressing is spread through the salad; it will look cohesive rather than loose. Avoid overmixing, which can break up the chicken.
Everything is coated now. How do I season it without overdoing the feta?
Taste a small spoonful first, since feta can be salty. Add salt only if it needs it, then add pepper to taste and stir once more to blend the seasoning.
It tastes balanced. Can I put it out now, or should it chill first?
You can serve it immediately. If lunch is later, cover it and refrigerate until serving, then give it a gentle stir and taste once more before putting it out.
For the Broccoli Coleslaw dressing, go with the first of the two sauce versions we discussed earlier.
Understood—I'll use the first version for the dressing and keep that choice in place as we make the coleslaw.
Yes, that's the one. I don't want to revisit the choice tonight; please just guide me through the Broccoli Coleslaw.
Absolutely. We'll stick with that dressing version and focus on getting everything prepped and ready to serve.
I have a small bowl, a large salad bowl, and a whisk out. What should I measure for the dressing?
Measure 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1/2 cup white sugar. Also set aside the seasoning packet from 1 (3 ounce) package of chicken flavored ramen noodles.
The oil, vinegar, sugar, and ramen seasoning are in the small bowl. How thoroughly should I mix it?

Whisk until the sugar and seasoning are well distributed through the oil and vinegar. Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour, or leave it overnight if you are preparing ahead.
While that chills, what goes into the large bowl?
Combine the diced broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds in the large bowl. Toss them enough to spread the vegetables and seeds evenly.
I still have the ramen block on the counter. Should it go in with the vegetables?
Yes. Crush the ramen noodles and stir them into the broccoli mixture. The seasoning packet belongs in the chilled dressing, not in the salad bowl.
Dinner is about an hour away. When should I bring the dressing and salad together?

Once the dressing has chilled for at least 1 hour, pour it over the salad about 10 minutes before serving. Toss so the broccoli, carrots, green onions, sunflower seeds, and crushed noodles are coated.
If I assemble it 10 minutes ahead, what should I look for before putting it on the table?

Check that the sugar-based dressing is evenly mixed through the vegetables and that the ramen pieces are distributed rather than clumped in one spot. Give the bowl a final gentle toss if dressing has settled at the bottom.
The salad is coated and the noodles are still noticeable. Is there anything else to do before serving?
That is ready to serve. Taste a small portion for the balance of sweet, tangy dressing and make sure the vegetables, seeds, and noodles are evenly spread through the Broccoli Coleslaw.
I'm making Grandmas Gingersnaps. Can you keep me on track from setup through shaping the cookies?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and have a medium bowl, a mixer or sturdy spoon, and ungreased cookie sheets ready.
What ingredients should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. Keep the egg and molasses nearby for after the margarine and sugar are creamed.
The margarine is softened. How should the sugar mixture look before I add anything else?
Cream the margarine with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture is smooth and evenly blended, without obvious lumps of margarine.
It looks smooth now. Should the egg and molasses go in together?
Yes. Beat in the egg and molasses until the color is even and the mixture looks well blended.
While that mixes, what dry ingredients should I have ready?
Gather 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon ground ginger, plus the cinnamon, baking soda, and salt called for in your recipe.
The molasses mixture is uniform. How do I combine the dry ingredients without making the dough tough?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt, then stir them into the molasses mixture just until a dough forms. Stop once you no longer see dry streaks.
My dough has come together. What texture am I aiming for before I portion it?
It should hold together as a workable dough rather than look wet or pourable. Roll it into 1 inch balls, then coat the balls in the sugar reserved for rolling if you have it ready.
The balls are shaped. How should I arrange them for the oven?
Place them 2 inches apart on the ungreased cookie sheets, then bake in the preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) oven according to the recipe's baking direction.
Let's work through Atomic Canuck Chili today. Where should I begin?

Yes. Set out a large skillet, a slow cooker, a stirring spoon, and a safe way to drain the browned beef. For the skillet portion, measure 2 pounds lean ground beef, 1/2 large diced onion, 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper, 3 tablespoons garlic powder, and 1 tablespoon seasoned pepper.
I have the beef and seasonings ready. Which slow-cooker ingredients should be on the counter?

Have 2 (4 ounce) cans of mushroom pieces drained, along with baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, barbeque sauce, and hot sauce. Keeping the kidney-bean liquid is important for the mixture.
The skillet is heating. What goes in together?

Over medium heat, brown the ground beef with the diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper. Break up the beef as it cooks so the seasonings and onion are distributed throughout.
The beef is browned and the onion has softened. Should I drain it before using the slow cooker?
Yes. Carefully drain off the fat, then transfer the beef-and-onion mixture to the slow cooker.
The meat is in the slow cooker. I want to add everything else without missing anything.

Stir in the drained mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce. Mix until the tomato paste is worked through the chili rather than sitting in a lump.
It is mixed and looks fairly thick. When do the final spicy ingredients go in?
Add the hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, then stir them through. The recipe calls for both at this stage, so make sure the heat is evenly blended before putting on the lid.
