No additional ingredient is specified at this point. The listed components—1 chuck roast, the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt—are already accounted for in the marinade and roast preparation.
I'm making Fire Side Coffee as a dry mix. What tools should I set out before I measure?
Have measuring cups and spoons, a sifter or fine sieve, a mixing bowl, a spoon, and a clean jar with a lid ready. Keep the jar dry so the mix stays free-flowing.
Which of the larger ingredients go into the bowl?
Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix into the bowl.
I have those measured. What are the remaining amounts?

Add 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon. The written sifting instruction also mentions nutmeg, but no nutmeg amount appears in the ingredient list, so check the original recipe if you have one rather than guessing a quantity.
Should the dry ingredients look completely uniform before I store them?

Sift the measured dry ingredients together until the cinnamon is evenly dispersed and there are no obvious clumps of creamer or hot chocolate mix. If you are using nutmeg, include only the amount specified by your recipe source.
The mixture is smooth and dry. How should I pack it away?
Transfer it to the clean jar, then seal the lid securely. A tightly closed jar helps keep moisture out of the mix.
I'm ready to make one mug. How much mix and water do I use?
Stir 3 teaspoons of the mixture into 1 cup of hot water. Keep stirring until the powders dissolve and the drink looks evenly blended.
It has dissolved, but I want to make sure the flavor is right before serving.
Taste it while it is still hot, then adjust to taste. Stir again after any adjustment so the cup remains smooth.

Make sure no dry powder is settled at the bottom, give the mug one last stir, and serve it hot.
I'm making Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2. What should I put on the counter before I start mixing?

Set out a large mixing bowl, a sturdy spoon or mixer, and the butter so it is softened. Measure 1 cup butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil; those are the ingredients used to begin the dough.
The butter is soft and the sugars and oil are measured. Do they all go into the bowl together?

It looks smooth, though a little fluffy around the sides of the bowl. What comes after creaming?
Add the eggs and vanilla, then mix well. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl so the egg does not remain in separate patches.

Stir just until the flour mixture is incorporated and you no longer see dry pockets. Stop once the dough comes together; avoid continuing to beat it simply to make it extra smooth.
The dough is uniform now. I have pecans, but not everyone wants them. Where do they fit in?

Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top?

Yes. You'll need a large pot, a strainer, and a container large enough to chill the finished tea. Set aside 1 pound fresh or frozen cranberries, 3 quarts cold water, 2 cups orange juice, and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice.
The cranberries are frozen, and I have the pot and strainer ready. Do they need thawing?
No thawing is needed. Put the frozen cranberries directly into the large pot with the 3 quarts of cold water.
That is on the stove. What am I looking for once it heats up?
Bring it to a boil, then cook only until the berries pop, about 5 minutes. You should see many of the cranberries split; there is no need to keep boiling them after that.
Most of the berries have popped, and the liquid is bright red. Should I strain it while it is hot?
Take the pot off the heat and leave it at room temperature until the mixture is cold, which will take several hours. Letting it cool before straining gives the cranberry liquid time to settle.
While it cools, what else should I measure and keep ready?

Measure the 2 cups orange juice, 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, and 1/4 cup lemon juice. Have the sugar ready as well, along with the cinnamon stick, whole cloves, and allspice berries called for in your recipe.
The cranberry mixture is cold now. How fine should I strain it?
Pour it through your strainer to remove the cranberries. Pressing very hard is unnecessary; let the liquid drain, then discard the solids.
I have a clear cranberry liquid in the serving container. What gets mixed in?
Stir in the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar until the sugar dissolves. Then add the cinnamon stick, whole cloves, and allspice berries.
Before I pour it for guests, what should I check?
Make sure the tea is fully cold, the sugar is dissolved, and the flavors are evenly stirred through. Remove any whole spices before serving if you do not want them in the cups.
I'm making Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms tonight. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I turn on the stove?

The vegetables are chopped and the stock is ready. What pan and utensil should I use?
Use a wide, heavy pan or skillet for the risotto and a wooden spoon or silicone spatula for steady stirring. Keep a bowl beside the stove for the sautéed vegetables when they come out of the pan.
The pan is warming. What goes in first?
Melt the butter, then add the Broccoflower, wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic. Sauté everything for 10 minutes, stirring often enough that the garlic does not catch on the pan.
At the end of the 10 minutes, what should the vegetables look like?

The onion should be softened, the mushrooms should have released much of their moisture, and the Broccoflower should be tendering at the edges. Transfer the sautéed mixture to the bowl and set it aside.
The pan is empty except for the cooking residue. Should I add the rice directly to it?
Yes. Add the 3 cups Arborio rice to that same pan. Begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until each addition is well incorporated before pouring in the next cup.
How will I know when it is time for another cup of stock?
Wait until the previous cup is mostly absorbed and the rice looks creamy rather than soupy. Keep stirring so the rice cooks evenly, then add the next 1-cup portion of stock.
The rice is nearly tender and the stock is absorbed. What should I season it with?
Stir in the nutmeg and herbs, then season with salt and pepper. The rice should be tender with a slight bite and have a loose, creamy consistency.
When do the mushrooms and Broccoflower return to the pan?
Once the risotto is cooked, fold the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic back in. Stir gently until they are warmed through, then taste for salt and pepper.
It is creamy and hot. Is there anything left before serving?
Stir in Parmesan cheese just before serving. Give it a final taste, make sure the vegetables are distributed throughout the risotto, and serve while it is warm.
I'm making Beet and Pear Puree today. Can you help me set up before I start?
Set out a roasting pan, a large skillet, a knife and cutting board, and a bowl or plate for the beets while they cool. Heat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Which produce should I prep while the oven heats?
Wash 8 medium beets. Also peel, core, and mince 4 Bosc pears, and mince 1 1/2 cups Vidalia onions.
I have the beets in the roasting pan. What else needs to be measured for the skillet?
Measure 1 pound unsalted butter, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and 1/2 cup cranberry vinegar. Keep them near the skillet with the minced onion and pears.

Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until they are tender when pierced. Then set them aside until they are cool enough to handle.
At the 45-minute mark, one beet gives easily to a knife but the larger ones still feel firm. Should I leave the pan in?
Yes. Continue roasting until the larger beets are tender too; the full range is 45 minutes to 1 hour. Let them cool after roasting rather than trying to peel them hot.
The beets are cooling. What should I do at the stove?
Melt the 1 pound of unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat.

Stir in the minced Vidalia onions, minced Bosc pears, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and 1/2 cup cranberry vinegar. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring frequently.
The pear-onion mixture has been cooking and looks soft. How should I handle the cooled beets before serving?
Once the beets are cool enough to handle, peel them and coarsely chop them. Check that the beets are tender and that the pear-onion mixture has cooked for the full 20 minutes before serving.

I'm making Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me gather the ingredients in a sensible order?
Start with 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, and 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta cheese.

Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, omitting salt and fat, then drain them well. Lay them out carefully so they do not stick together or tear.

Stir the ricotta, shredded Monterey Jack, drained green chiles, chili powder, and salt together until the mixture is evenly combined.

I'm about to start Fruit Dip 2. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. This is a chilled, no-cook dip, so have a mixing bowl, a sturdy spoon or hand mixer, measuring cups, and a cover for the bowl ready.

Set out 8 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, 2 cups frozen whipped topping that has fully thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice.

It will blend more smoothly if it has softened somewhat. Let it sit briefly if needed, then combine it with the marshmallow creme and thawed whipped topping.
Should I pour in all of the pineapple juice while I'm mixing those?

Start by blending the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and whipped topping until the mixture is smooth and evenly combined. Add pineapple juice afterward, only as needed to reach a dip-able consistency.
The base is smooth, but it seems quite thick. How should I add the juice?

Chill the dip for 1 hour so it can firm up and the flavors can settle.
The hour is up and I'm about to set out the fruit. Should I stir the dip again?
Give it a gentle stir and check that it is still creamy and easy to dip into. Transfer it to a serving bowl if you like, then serve it chilled alongside the fruit.

Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon and transfer it to paper towels. That drains excess grease while leaving the rendered fat behind in the skillet.

I'm about to make A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie. What should I put out before I start?

Should I thaw the mixed berries first, or use them straight from the freezer?
Use the berries frozen. They are meant to go into the blender with the drained peaches and honey, and they will help give the smoothie a thick, cold texture.

Add the frozen mixed berries, then the drained sliced peaches, and pour in the 2 tablespoons honey. All three ingredients can go into the blender together.

It is blending, but the frozen fruit is moving slowly around the blades. What texture am I aiming for?

Great, I'm ready to pour it into glasses.
Pour the smoothie promptly while it is cold and thick. This recipe is complete once the frozen mixed berries, drained peaches, and honey have been blended until smooth.
I want to make Cinnamon Crackle Cookies. I have a mixing bowl and baking sheets out—what ingredients should I set beside me?

The butter, shortening, and both sugars are measured. Should I start combining them now?
Yes. Put the butter, shortening, sugar, and packed brown sugar in the mixing bowl and cream them together. Scrape down the bowl as needed so no pockets of shortening or brown sugar remain.
What should the creamed mixture look like before I add anything else?
It should look evenly blended and lighter in texture, without obvious lumps of butter, shortening, or packed brown sugar.

I'm putting together asparagus sandwiches for a light lunch. I have a 10 ounce can of asparagus tips—what should I do with them before assembling?
Drain the asparagus tips well, then lay the spears on paper towels. Let the towels draw off excess liquid so the bread will not become soggy.

Spread a thin, even coating over each slice. Cover the surface without piling it on, since too much filling can squeeze out when you roll the sandwiches.

Set one asparagus spear on a prepared bread slice, near one edge. Position it straight across the slice so the roll stays even.

Roll the slice snugly around the spear, using gentle pressure to hold its shape without flattening the bread. Place the seam underneath when you set it down.
