I'm about to make Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup, but I haven't decided how I want to handle the finishing liquid and starch yet.
There are two workable ways to keep in mind. First, hold back extra liquid and use a small final splash to loosen the starches. Second, keep the extra liquid separate and add it at serving.
Please keep those two possibilities in that first-then-second order in my notes. I want to see how the soup feels before I decide.
Absolutely. We can keep both options open while you cook, without treating either one as your decision yet.
Before I turn on the burner, what should I put within reach?
Set out a large pot, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, and 1 medium chopped onion. Have a spoon ready for stirring.
What else should I prep beside the pot?
Keep the chopped green bell pepper, 1 large carrot that is peeled and thinly sliced, and the garlic ready to go. Also bring out the black beans, chicken broth, and a blender for later.
My pot is in place and the oil is measured. How should I start?
Warm the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat. Once it is hot, you can add the vegetables.
The oil is warm. What should I watch for while the vegetables cook?
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and garlic. Cook them for 5 minutes, stirring as needed, until the vegetables are tender.
Once the carrot has softened, when do the beans and broth go in?
After the vegetables are tender, mix in 1 can of black beans and the chicken broth. Stir well so the vegetables and beans are evenly distributed.
What is the intended use for the remaining can of beans?
Put the remaining can of beans in the blender and puree them until smooth.
Before I take the soup off the stove or set it out, what should I check?

Check the taste and texture, and make sure the pureed beans are smooth. If you want to revisit the liquid question at serving, your two options remain in the same order: a small final splash to loosen the starches, or extra liquid kept separate for serving.

source_seed.recipe_title: Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup

messages.content: I'm about to make Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs. Should I get the oven going while I chop the vegetables?
Yes—preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Set a medium saucepan on the stove as well, so it is ready once your chopping is done.
What ingredients should I measure and prep before I turn on the burner?

Have 2 tablespoons olive oil ready, along with 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove garlic, crushed. The directions also call for cayenne pepper; use the amount specified in your recipe notes, since no quantity is included here.
My mushrooms are chopped, the green onions are sliced, and the garlic is crushed. Is the pan the right place to start?
Pour the olive oil into the medium saucepan and heat it over medium heat. Give it a moment to warm before adding the vegetables.
How can I tell whether the oil is warm enough without letting it smoke?
It should look loose and glossy across the bottom of the pan. If it begins smoking, lower the heat briefly before you add anything.
The oil is shimmering lightly. What goes in, and should I stir constantly?
Add the chopped mushrooms, green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper. Stir them together so the garlic and onions are distributed through the mushrooms, then stir occasionally as they cook.
The pan looks quite full with the 3 cups of mushrooms. Will that affect the cooking time?
The mushrooms will release moisture and shrink as they cook. Keep the heat at medium and let them cook for 10 minutes, stirring from time to time so the mixture cooks evenly.
At the 10-minute mark, what texture am I looking for before serving?
The mushrooms and green onions should be tender, and the garlic should smell cooked rather than sharp or raw. If the mushrooms are still firm, continue only until they are tender.
The vegetables are tender and the pan smells garlicky and savory. Is there anything to check before I bring out the Mushroom Puffs?

Taste the mushroom mixture carefully for seasoning and confirm that no pieces of garlic or mushroom remain undercooked. With the oven already at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), your cooked filling is ready for the next serving or assembly step provided with the puffs.
Before I start the Frosted Shortbread, I'm undecided about the fruit seasoning detail.
You could keep two possibilities open: first, use a light cardamom-and-ginger note with the fruit; second, use cinnamon as the only warm spice.
Please leave those two options in that order in my notes. I'll decide later, after I see what feels right.
Absolutely—we'll treat them as two open possibilities and won't settle on either one today.
While that stays open, what should I set on the counter for the dough?
Set out a mixing bowl, a greased 15-in pan, 1 cup softened butter with no substitutes, and 1 cup packed brown sugar.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. What else should be ready before I mix?
Have 1 egg yolk and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract ready. Keep the flour and salt together separately until the creamed mixture is ready for them.
Should I grease the pan before I begin mixing?
Yes. Grease the 15-in pan now, then cream the softened butter and packed brown sugar together in the mixing bowl.
What should the butter and sugar look like before I add anything else?
Keep mixing until the butter and brown sugar are thoroughly blended into an even, creamy mixture, without separate streaks of butter.
It's creamy now. How do the yolk and vanilla go in?
Add the 1 egg yolk and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, then mix well so they are fully incorporated.
The mixture is smooth again. When do I bring in the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour and salt, then add them to the creamed mixture. Mix just until the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is together and the pan is greased. What is the last thing I should do?
Press the dough into the greased 15-in pan, spreading it into an even layer and checking that it reaches the edges consistently.
I'm making Chocolate Chews and want to set up before I start heating anything. What ingredients are listed?

The ingredient list has 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. The directions also mention eggs, but the ingredient list does not give an egg quantity.
I found the chocolate chips and butter. Should both be measured out now?
Yes. Measure 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips and set out 1/2 cup softened butter. Keep the chips near a heavy saucepan and the butter in a mixing bowl or beside it for creaming.
What else should be on the counter?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Have a spoon or heatproof spatula ready for the chocolate and a mixer or sturdy spoon for the butter and sugars.
The chips are in my heavy saucepan. How gently should I heat them?
Use very low heat. Stir the chips as they warm so they melt evenly, scraping the bottom and sides of the heavy saucepan to prevent scorching.
Some of the chips are still holding their shape, but the mixture is glossy around them.

Keep stirring over very low heat until the chocolate is evenly melted and no firm chip pieces remain. The recipe's next mixing task is separate from the saucepan: creaming the butter with both sugars.
I'm at the bowl with the softened butter and the two sugars. What texture am I aiming for?

Cream the butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar together until the mixture looks light and fluffy rather than dense or streaky. Scrape the bowl once or twice so the butter and sugars combine evenly.
The butter-sugar mixture is pale and fluffy. The directions say to add eggs, but my ingredient list does not say how many.

The directions specify beating in the eggs one at a time, but they do not provide a number. Check the complete recipe card or source for that missing quantity before adding them; after each egg, beat until it is incorporated before adding the next.
Once the eggs are incorporated, is there a baking or finishing direction on this card?

Not in the instructions provided. They cover melting and stirring the chocolate, creaming the butter and sugars, and beating in eggs one at a time, but they do not state when to combine components, add other ingredients, bake, or serve. Confirm the rest of the recipe before proceeding.
I'm making Apple Pie 2 today. What equipment and ingredients should I set out before I start?

Use a large pot and a long spoon for stirring. Gather 1 gallon apple juice, 1 gallon apple cider, 3 cups white sugar, and 8 cinnamon sticks. Keep the grain alcohol nearby but away from the stove; you will add it only after the juice mixture has cooled completely. Have the 750 milliliter bottle of 190-proof grain alcohol ready.
Everything is measured, and my large pot is on the stove. Do the cinnamon sticks go in right away?
Yes. Add the apple juice, apple cider, sugar, and all 8 cinnamon sticks to the pot. Stir as the pot heats so the sugar starts dissolving into the liquid.
The sugar is mostly disappearing, but the pot has not boiled yet. What am I watching for?
Keep heating until the mixture reaches a full boil. Once it boils, take the pot off the heat rather than continuing to cook it.
It just came to a boil, so I removed it from the burner. Should I cover it while it cools?
Let it cool completely before adding anything else. The cinnamon can remain in the pot while the mixture cools; the important point is that the liquid is no longer warm when the alcohol goes in.
How can I tell when it is cool enough for the alcohol?
Wait until there is no heat or steam coming off the pot and the mixture is completely cool. Adding the grain alcohol before then would not follow the recipe's cooling step.
The mixture is fully cool now, and the cinnamon sticks are still floating in it. What do I do next?
Stir in the 750 milliliter bottle of 190-proof grain alcohol until the drink is evenly combined. Stir steadily enough to distribute it throughout the apple-and-cinnamon mixture.
It looks uniform after stirring. Is there anything I should check before serving it?
Make sure the sugar is fully dissolved, the cinnamon sticks are distributed through the mixture, and the grain alcohol has been stirred in evenly. Once those checks look good, it is ready to serve.
I'm ready to pour it. Should I leave the cinnamon sticks in?
You can leave the cinnamon sticks in for serving, since they are part of the recipe. Pour carefully from the cooled pot, and keep any remaining mixture in a suitable covered container.
I have the salmon out and want to set up the pan before I handle the crumb mixture. Which pan should I use?
Use a 15-in baking pan. Line it with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray so the salmon is easy to lift off later.
Before I get further into Baked Salmon with Herbs, I am still undecided about how I want the soft herbs to look.

Either presentation can work. First, leave the soft herbs in larger leaves and set them in a small pile at one edge of the bowl. Second, chop the soft herbs finely, fold half into the warm food, and scatter the rest at the end.
Please keep those two Baked Salmon with Herbs options in that first-and-second order in my notes. I want to see how the dish looks before deciding.
Absolutely—we can leave both possibilities open in that order while you cook, without treating either one as your decision.
What ingredients should I measure near the bowl for the topping?
Set out 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese, and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes. Have the thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper nearby as well.
The crumbs, garlic, cheese, and seasonings are ready. How should the mixture look before the butter goes in?

Combine the bread crumbs, garlic, Parmesan, parsley, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper in the bowl. Stir until the garlic and seasonings are spread through the crumbs rather than sitting in separate spots.
It is evenly mixed but still dry and loose. What do I do with the butter?
Add the butter and toss the mixture until it coats the crumbs evenly. Look for a uniformly moistened crumb mixture, without a few heavily buttered clumps.
My foil-lined pan is ready and the crumb mixture is coated. Where does the salmon go?
Place the salmon on the prepared pan, keeping it on the sprayed foil so it does not stick.
When it has baked according to the rest of my recipe, what should I check before serving?

Use the baking time and temperature provided with your recipe, then check that the salmon is opaque, flakes readily at its thickest point, and reaches 145°F in the center. Make sure the crumb topping is in place before serving.
Once it is plated, I will decide whether either soft-herb idea suits it. Is there anything else to do right away?

Let the salmon rest briefly for easier serving, then remove the foil from the pan for quick cleanup. The two soft-herb presentations can remain open options: the larger leaves first, and the finely chopped, half-folded and half-scattered version second.
I'm about to make Black Bean Chili, and I want to leave one chili-detail undecided while I cook.

Either approach can work. First, add the chili as a late streak over only part of the finished dish. Second, bloom a small amount of chili in the oil at the beginning and leave off any extra chili on top.
Please keep those two Black Bean Chili possibilities in that exact order in my notes. I'll decide which feels right later.
Absolutely—I'll treat them as two open possibilities for this batch, with no decision made yet.
Before I turn on the stove, what should I set beside my large saucepan?
Have 1 tablespoon olive oil and the chopped onion closest to the pan. Keep a spoon handy for stirring, and place the remaining prepared vegetables nearby so they can go in together.
I have the onion ready. Which vegetables should be prepped before the pan gets hot?
Prepare 2 red bell peppers, seeded and chopped, plus 1 jalapeno pepper, seeded and minced. The sauté also uses mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn, so have those ready before you begin.
The saucepan is on the burner. How hot should I make it for the oil?
Warm the olive oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat. Let the pan heat through, but do not let the oil smoke.
The oil is hot and the onion is ready to go in. What am I looking for as the vegetables cook?

Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn. Sauté for 10 minutes, or until the onion turns translucent, stirring often enough to keep the vegetables from catching on the bottom.
The onion is softening and the pan smells sweet. When do the dry seasonings go in?
Season the vegetables with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder at this point. Stir well so the spices coat the mixture; the two chili presentation ideas remain open rather than being chosen now.
I've got the beans and broth beside the stove. What joins the vegetables next?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Mix until the beans are evenly distributed and the bottom of the saucepan is clear of any stuck seasoning.
While working on Black Bean Chili, before I ladle it into bowls, what should I check?
Taste for salt, check that the beans are heated through, and make sure the chili has the texture you want. You can then serve it as is while still leaving the two chili-detail options undecided.
I have a large pot and cutting board ready for Chicken and Black Bean Chili. What should I keep within reach before the burner goes on?
Set out 2 tablespoons cooking oil, 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces, sea salt, and 1 tablespoon chili powder. Keep a spoon handy for stirring in the pot.
The chicken is cut up. Which of the seasonings and vegetables should I pull out now?

Have 1/2 tablespoon ground cumin and 1 dried chipotle chili pepper, ground into powder, ready with black pepper and cayenne pepper. You will also need onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper.
Everything is measured and chopped. My empty pot is over medium heat.
Add the oil to the pot and let it heat over medium heat. When it moves easily across the bottom of the pot, add the chicken pieces in an even layer.
The chicken is sizzling, but a few pieces are still pale on top. Should I season it already?

Give the chicken time to brown on all sides first, turning the pieces as needed. Once the outside is browned, season it with sea salt, chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
The chicken is browned and I have stirred in the spices. It smells quite smoky from the chipotle.
That is expected from the ground chipotle. Stir for a moment so the seasonings coat the chicken evenly and do not sit in dry clumps on the bottom of the pot.
The spices are coating the chicken evenly. When do the peppers and onion go in?
Add the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, then mix them through the seasoned chicken. Keep stirring enough to distribute the vegetables throughout the pot.
The vegetables are mixed in, and the pot looks less wet than I expected. What should I watch for from here?
Pour in about 3 cups water and continue cooking for 10 minutes, until about 1/2 of the water has evaporated. The useful cue is a reduced, less watery mixture rather than rushing the reduction.
The liquid has reduced by about half. I have the kidney beans, black beans, and corn ready beside the pot.
Mix the kidney beans, black beans, and corn into the chili. Before serving, taste for salt and chili powder, and check that the chicken, vegetables, beans, and corn are evenly distributed.
I'm making Almond Buttercrunch. What should I arrange before I turn on the stove?

Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup chopped almonds beside a saucepan. Have 2 cups milk chocolate chips ready near a large buttered cookie sheet, plus a candy thermometer and a small bowl of cold water for checking the syrup.
I have both 1-cup and 1/2-cup measures out. Which amount of almonds goes into the candy?
Measure 1 cup of chopped almonds for the candy; do not use only 1/2 cup. Keep the butter and sugar measured as well so everything can go into the pan together.
The cookie sheet is buttered and the pan is on the stove. What goes in now?
Over low heat, combine the butter, sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds in the saucepan. Stir constantly while the butter melts and the sugar mixture comes up to a boil.
It has started bubbling across the surface. Should I keep stirring?
Once it boils, stop stirring and do not shake the pan. Let the candy cook undisturbed while you monitor the temperature.
I'm watching the thermometer. What temperature am I aiming for, and is there another way to confirm it?
Cook the syrup to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. As a backup check, a small amount dropped into cold water should form hard, brittle threads.
It has reached the hard-crack stage. Where should the hot candy go?
Carefully pour it onto the large buttered cookie sheet and let it spread out. Work carefully because the syrup is extremely hot.
The candy is on the sheet and still hot. When do the chocolate chips get used?
Immediately press the 2 cups milk chocolate chips onto the hot candy. As they soften and melt, spread them into an even chocolate coating over the surface.
The chocolate is mostly smooth. Is there anything else to do before serving?
Sprinkle finely chopped almonds over the chocolate coating, then let the buttercrunch cool completely. Once firm, break it into uneven pieces and check that the chocolate is set before serving.
I have the 3 pounds of beef roast ready. What should I do while the oven heats?
Set the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). While it preheats, get out a large roasting pan and a large bowl.
The pan is ready. Does the roast go in before the onions?
Yes. Place the roast in the large roasting pan, then scatter the 2 chopped onions over it.
Should I make the sauce separately, or pour everything over the beef as I measure it?
Mix it separately in the large bowl. Combine the Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper there before adding the beer.
How much Worcestershire sauce should I measure, and what beer quantity do I need?
Measure 6 teaspoons of Worcestershire sauce. Use 2 cans or bottles of beer, each 12 fluid ounces.
The roast is covered with onions, and the seasoning mixture is in the bowl. What comes next?
Pour the beer into the bowl, stir the mixture, and then add it to the roasting pan with the roast and onions.
Do I need to stir the onions into the liquid once it is in the pan?
A thorough stir before adding the mixture is enough. Once it is in the pan, make sure the roast, onions, and beer mixture are together in the roasting pan.
The oven has reached 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Is the pan ready to go in?
Yes. With the beer mixture added to the roast and onions, place the roasting pan in the preheated oven.
Should I add water or any extra liquid before it cooks?
No extra water is listed in these instructions. Use the beer mixture as prepared, and follow the recipe's cooking directions without adding another liquid.
I'm making Baked Fettuccine Lasagna and want to get the water going before I prep anything else. What should I set out?
Set out a large pot, a colander, and 12 ounces of dry fettuccine. You'll also want lightly salted water ready for the pot. Bring the water to a boil while you gather the other ingredients.
What ingredients should be beside the stove for the meat and vegetable parts?
Have 1 pound lean ground beef, if you're using the optional beef, plus 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper ready. A large skillet and a bowl for the cooked meat will be useful too.
The pot is boiling. How long should the fettuccine cook?
Add the fettuccine and cook it for 8 to 10 minutes, until al dente. Drain it thoroughly in the colander when it is tender but still has a little firmness.
While the pasta drains, can I start the beef?
Yes. Put the beef in the large skillet and brown it over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks. It should lose its pink color and cook into small, separated pieces.
The beef is browned, but there is fat in the skillet. What do I do with it?
Drain the fat from the pan, then transfer the browned meat to a bowl. Keep the skillet available for the vegetables.
What goes into the skillet after I move the meat?
Cook the chopped onion and red bell pepper in the same skillet with 1 tablespoon butter until the vegetables are tender. Stir occasionally so the onion softens and the pepper cooks evenly.
How will I know the onion and pepper are tender enough?
The onion should look softened rather than crisp, and the bell pepper should give easily when stirred or pressed with a spoon. Avoid letting either vegetable remain firm and raw-tasting.
The pasta is drained, the beef is in a bowl, and the vegetables are soft. Is there anything else in these directions before serving?

Those are the cooking steps provided: boil and drain the fettuccine, brown and drain the optional beef, then soften the onion and bell pepper in butter. Check the remaining recipe directions for any assembly or baking details before serving, since they are not included here.
I'm making Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2 and have a large mixing bowl and a saucepan ready. What ingredients should I measure first?
Measure the dry ingredients into the mixing bowl: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The flour, sugar, cinnamon, and salt are in the bowl. Should I mix them before I use the saucepan?
Yes. Stir or whisk the dry ingredients together so the cinnamon and salt are evenly distributed, then leave the bowl nearby.
What goes into the saucepan for the chocolate mixture?
Combine 1 cup water, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, the butter, and the cocoa in the saucepan. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, stirring as needed so the cocoa blends in.
The cocoa mixture has reached a steady boil. What do I do with the dry bowl?
Carefully pour the hot cocoa mixture over the dry ingredients. Mix well, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl until there are no dry pockets.
The batter is combined but still warm. Which additions come next?
Add the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda. Mix well again, until the batter looks smooth and evenly blended.
It looks smooth now. How should I prepare the baking pan?
Grease and flour a 15-in pan, then pour in the batter and spread it into an even layer.
Before I continue with Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2, my oven is heating. What temperature and bake time should I use?
Bake at 375 degrees F for 15-20 minutes. Start checking near the shorter end of the time so the cake does not overbake.
When I check the center, what tells me it is ready to come out?
Insert a toothpick near the center. The cake is done when the toothpick comes out clean. If it has wet batter on it, keep baking briefly and check again before serving.
I'm getting ready for Diegos Special Beef Stew. Can you help me sequence the steps?
Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, a resealable plastic bag, a skillet, and a slow cooker. You will also need 2 tablespoons olive oil for browning.
I see 2 teaspoons butter as well. Should that go into the bag with the beef and flour?
No. Put only the cubed beef and the 1 tablespoon flour in the resealable bag. Keep the butter aside; the listed steps do not call for adding it during the flour-coating stage.
Do I need 1/4 cup of liquid or anything else before I start heating the skillet?
No 1/4 cup ingredient is listed for these steps. For this portion of the stew, focus on the beef, flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and the slow cooker.
The bag is sealed. How thoroughly should I shake it?
Shake and turn the sealed bag until the flour is evenly distributed over the beef cubes. The pieces should look lightly coated rather than sitting in a clump of loose flour.
The beef is coated. My skillet is on the stove—what goes in?
Heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the floured beef in a layer that gives the pieces room to brown.
Some sides are browned, but a few pieces are still pale. Should I move them around?
Turn the pieces as needed so the remaining pale sides contact the skillet. Keep the heat at medium and continue until the beef is browned on all sides.
The beef has color all around, and there are browned bits in the skillet. Is it ready for the slow cooker?
Yes. Transfer all of the browned beef to the slow cooker. Make sure the beef leaves the skillet safely and the cooker is ready for the next recipe steps.
Before I continue, should I add the 2 teaspoons butter to the slow cooker?

The ingredient list includes 2 teaspoons butter, but the supplied instructions only direct you to coat the beef, brown it in olive oil, and transfer it to the slow cooker. Hold the butter until a later recipe direction specifies where to use it.
I'm making Carrot and Coriander Soup II. I have a large saucepan and a blender ready; can you help me keep the steps on track?
Yes. Gather 4 large carrots cut into 1 inch pieces, 1/4 large onion chopped, 1 quart vegetable broth, and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro.
The carrots are cut and the onion and cilantro are chopped. Do any of those need to be cooked separately?
No separate sautéing is needed. Put the carrots, onion, vegetable broth, and cilantro together in the large saucepan.
Everything is in the pan, and the broth just covers the vegetables. Should I cover it while it heats?
Heat the pan until the soup comes to a boil. Once boiling, cook it until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
It has been simmering for several minutes. What is the best way to tell whether the carrot pieces are ready?
Pierce a carrot piece with a fork or the tip of a knife. It should yield easily without a firm center; if it does, take the saucepan off the heat.
The carrots are soft now. Can I blend it right away?
Let the soup cool slightly first. That makes it safer to puree and helps prevent hot soup from splashing out of the blender or food processor.
The steam has eased. I'm using a blender—what texture am I aiming for?
Puree the soup until it is smooth, with no noticeable carrot chunks. If your blender is small, blend in batches and return the soup to the pan as needed.
It is smooth and looks fairly thick. Should I cook it again before serving?
Reheat it only if it has cooled more than you want for serving. Give it a stir while warming so the smooth puree heats evenly.
Before I ladle it into bowls, what final check should I make?
Check that the soup is hot, fully smooth, and that the carrot flavor and fresh cilantro are evenly distributed throughout the bowl.
I'm planning BBQ Chuck Roast for tomorrow. Can you help me get the marinade ready tonight?

Set out the 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. You'll also need the garlic, fresh ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt called for in the marinade.
I have the roast and liquids on the counter. How much garlic and ginger should I prep?
Prepare 3 teaspoons minced garlic and 3 teaspoons thinly sliced fresh ginger root. Have a large bowl ready so you can mix the marinade before adding the roast.
The bowl is ready. Do the sauces and beer go in together?
Yes. Combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt in the large bowl, and stir until the seasonings are dispersed through the liquid.
The marinade is mixed and the roast is in it. What should I do before refrigerating?
Make sure the roast is coated, cover the bowl, and refrigerate it for six hours. Turn the roast often during that time so the marinade contacts all sides.
The roast has marinated for six hours. Should I start the grill before taking it out?
Preheat the outdoor grill for indirect heat. While it heats, remove the roast from the marinade and transfer the used marinade to a saucepan rather than discarding it.
The roast is out and the marinade is in a saucepan. Is it okay to use that later on the grill?
Yes, after bringing the marinade to a boil and cooking it for 5 minutes. That makes it suitable to set aside as a basting sauce for the roast.
The sauce has boiled for 5 minutes and I've set it aside. How should I arrange the roast on the grill?
Place the chuck roast over the indirect-heat side of the grill rather than directly over the hottest coals or burners. Use the cooked marinade as basting sauce while it cooks.
While it grills, what should I watch for with the sauce and roast?

Keep the basting sauce in a separate clean container or pan, and brush it on as needed. Watch the roast's exterior for steady browning without scorching, since indirect heat is meant to cook it more gently.
I have dates and nuts ready for Date Nut Bars. Should I prepare the pan and oven before mixing?
Yes. Grease a 15-in pan and heat the oven to 350 degrees F so the stiff batter can go straight in once it is mixed.
What dry ingredients should I measure into my large bowl?
Measure 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Do the dates and nuts go in with those dry ingredients or later?
Add the dates and nuts to the large bowl with the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt, then combine them before adding the remaining ingredients.
The dry mixture is combined, and the fruit and nuts look evenly scattered through it. What do I add next?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; this batter is expected to be very stiff.
It is much thicker than a cake batter and takes effort to stir. Should I keep mixing until it turns smooth?
No. Once you no longer see dry flour, stop stirring. A dense, stiff mixture is the intended texture, so it does not need to become smooth or pourable.
How can I get that stiff batter into the prepared 15-in pan without overworking it?
Scrape it into the greased pan and spread it into an even layer with a spatula. Work just enough to level it across the pan.
The pan is in the oven. When should I begin checking the bars?
Bake at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes. Start checking near 20 minutes and continue only until the top is golden brown.
The top is golden brown at 22 minutes. Is that the readiness sign for these bars?
Yes. Golden brown is the recipe's doneness cue, so remove the pan once that color is reached within the 20-25 minute baking range and let the bars cool before serving.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip for a small gathering. Can you keep me on track while I prep?
Absolutely. Have a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish ready, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) before you start mixing.
I have the casserole dish out. Which chilled ingredients should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream into the casserole dish.
The mayonnaise and sour cream are in the dish. What pantry items need attention?
Add 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix. Drain and chop 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, then add those as well.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. I also have the cheese and crab meat ready; should they go in before baking?

Yes. Combine the mayonnaise, sour cream, soup mix, artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat directly in the casserole dish. Stir until the mixture is evenly blended and the artichokes are distributed throughout.
It is mixed, though I can still see distinct pieces of artichoke and crab. Is that okay?
That is fine—the dip does not need to be completely smooth. Just make sure there are no dry pockets of soup mix and that the ingredients are spread evenly through the creamy base.
My oven is at temperature. Do I cover the casserole?
Bake it uncovered for 30 minutes.
While it bakes, what should I look for when the timer is nearly done?
Look for a hot, cohesive dip with the surface set and gently bubbling around the edges. The 30-minute bake is the recipe timing, so keep it uncovered throughout.
The dip is hot and bubbling, and the surface has set. What is the serving move?
Serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it is hot and creamy.
I'm making Crab Cake Sauce to go with dinner. Can you guide me while I put it together?
Absolutely. This is a cold, blended sauce, so set out a blender, a spatula, and a container for chilling it afterward.
What ingredients should I measure before I start blending?
Measure 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa.
Those four are ready. The directions mention a few other things too—what do I need to check for?
Have cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt available as well. They are named in the blending directions, but no quantities are provided here, so don't assume amounts that aren't specified.
My blender is clean and everything is on the counter. Should I add the ingredients in a particular order?
Add the sour cream, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, hot salsa, cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt to the blender. Put the lid on securely, then puree until the sauce is smooth.
It is blending, but the cottage cheese is still making the sauce look a little grainy.
Keep blending until those curds disappear and the mixture looks uniform. Stop once or twice to scrape down the sides with a spatula if needed, then blend again.
The sauce is smooth now. Should it be served right away?
Chill it before serving. Transfer it to a covered container or cover the blender jar and refrigerate the sauce.
Before I refrigerate it, what should I look for?
Check that the sauce is evenly blended, with no visible streaks of sour cream, mayonnaise, or pockets of salsa. Wipe the rim clean so the cover sits properly.
It is covered and chilling. What will tell me it is ready to put out with the crab cakes?
Once chilled, it should still be smooth and spoonable. Give it a brief stir before serving if it has settled, then serve it alongside the crab cakes.
I have 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces ready for Coq au Vin alla Italiana. What should I set out before I touch the stove?

Keep a large skillet, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour within reach. Have a plate or tray ready for the floured chicken so you can transfer pieces to the pan without searching for space.
Should I prepare the flour before heating the skillet?
Yes. Season the 1/2 cup flour with poultry seasoning and mix it evenly. That way the coating is ready as soon as the pan is hot.
The seasoned flour is mixed. How should I start the pan?
Heat the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the large skillet, then add 1/2 of the crushed garlic. Let the garlic become fragrant without letting it darken.
The garlic is sizzling gently and still pale. Can I coat the chicken now?
Go ahead. Dredge the chicken pieces in the seasoned flour, shaking off any heavy excess so the coating is light rather than pasty.
I have several coated pieces ready. Do they all need to go into the skillet at once?
Add only the pieces that fit in a single layer with some room around them. The chicken needs direct contact with the skillet to brown instead of steaming.
What should I watch for while the chicken browns?
Brown the dredged chicken in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes. Look for a golden flour coating and steady sizzling; if it is browning too quickly, lower the heat slightly.
After 4 minutes, the underside is golden but a couple of pieces look lighter near the edges. Should I move them yet?

If the coating releases easily and is golden across most of the surface, turn or remove the pieces as needed. Give the lighter pieces the remaining minute so they have a chance to brown without scorching the garlic.
The chicken is browned and the skillet has some floury bits left behind. What should I check before I continue with the rest of the recipe?

Confirm that all of the chicken has been dredged and browned, that the garlic has not burned, and that the skillet still has enough space for the next ingredients. Keep the remaining 1/2 of the crushed garlic nearby for the later part of the dish.
I've got a large Dutch oven ready for Chicken and Herbs in White Wine. What should be on the counter before I heat it?
Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, the 1 (4 pound) chicken cut into pieces, garlic powder, and paper towels. Keep the sliced mushrooms nearby as well.
The chicken is portioned and the paper towels are on a plate. How should I begin?
Heat the olive oil in the Dutch oven over medium heat. While it warms, sprinkle the chicken pieces with garlic powder to taste.
The oil is hot and the chicken is seasoned. Am I looking for a deep crust right away?
Brown the chicken on both sides in the hot oil. Let each side take on color before turning it, rather than moving the pieces around constantly.
Both sides are browned, but there is plenty of fat left in the pot. Where does the chicken go?
Transfer the browned chicken to the paper towels. The towels will catch excess surface fat while you deal with the Dutch oven.
The chicken is resting on the towels. Should I keep that fat for the vegetables?
Spoon off the chicken fat, then return the Dutch oven to the stove. Leave the pan ready for the next ingredients rather than adding anything new at this point.
I'm ready to bring in the vegetables. Can you confirm what I need?
Have 1/2 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced, and 1 large onion, diced, ready. Keep 1/2 teaspoon dried basil close by too.
The mushrooms and diced onion are beside the stove. What texture should I aim for?
Stir the mushrooms and onions into the Dutch oven and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft. The mushrooms should soften as they cook alongside them.
The onions are soft and the mushrooms have cooked down. How should I handle the serving step?
Remove the cooked mixture to a medium bowl. Before serving, check that the chicken, mushrooms, and onions are distributed evenly and that the texture looks as you want it.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken and Herbs in White Wine

messages.content: I'm getting Baked Halibut Steaks ready. What equipment and ingredients should I set beside the stove?

Have a shallow baking dish, a medium saucepan, and a spoon ready. Measure 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1 cup diced zucchini, 1/2 cup minced onion, and 1 clove garlic, peeled and minced. Keep the tomatoes, basil, salt, pepper, and halibut steaks nearby for the later steps.
The vegetables are measured. Should I prepare the baking dish before I start the saucepan?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), then lightly grease the shallow baking dish. That leaves it ready when the vegetable mixture is done.
The oven is heating and the dish is greased. How should I cook the zucchini, onion, and garlic?
Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced zucchini, minced onion, and garlic, then cook and stir for 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
What should the vegetables look like when they are tender enough?
The zucchini and onion should be softened and easy to stir through, with the garlic fragrant. Stir regularly during the 5 minutes so the garlic does not sit in one hot spot.
The zucchini has softened and the onion is tender. Do the tomatoes go into the pan while it is still on the heat?
Remove the saucepan from the heat before adding them. Mix in the tomatoes, basil, salt, and pepper off the heat so the vegetables and seasonings are combined.
The tomato mixture is combined. Where do the halibut steaks go?
Arrange the halibut steaks in a single layer in the prepared shallow baking dish. Avoid stacking or overlapping them so each steak has its own space in the dish.
Should I check anything about the fish arrangement before I put the dish in the oven?

Make sure the steaks are lying flat in one layer and that the baking dish is still lightly greased. The directions provided end after arranging the halibut, so follow any remaining baking or serving details on your full recipe card.
The steaks are flat in the dish, and the vegetable mixture is ready beside them. Is there anything else from these directions I need to add?

You have covered the listed ingredients and preparation: the olive oil, zucchini, onion, garlic, tomatoes, basil, salt, pepper, and halibut steaks. The next action should come from any continuation of the recipe that gives the baking details.
Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes is next on my counter. Help me move through it without losing track of the recipe.
Certainly. We'll organize the ingredients first and then follow the cooking cues in order.
For the current stage of Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, which cue should guide the next move?
For the opening setup, have 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes; 2 medium zucchini, diced ready at the work area.
Before I handle the next part of Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, what should I prepare or inspect?
The next ingredients to stage are 1 teaspoon dried basil; 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley. Leave these items separate before the active cooking begins.
As I continue with Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, what belongs within reach now?
Add these: 1 9-ounce package refrigerated small cheese tortellini; 1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes; 2 medium zucchini, diced; 1 tsp. dried basil. Once that is done to read the texture.
Before I handle the next part of Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, which cue should guide the next move?
Then simmer for 10-20 minutes until tender. As the food changes, look for the recipe's intended visual cue.
With Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes in front of me, what should I prepare or inspect?
Before removing from heat, stir in 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley. Before moving on, confirm the doneness.
For the current stage of Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, what should I prepare or inspect?
Add salt and pepper, to taste. At that stage hold the completed preparation in place until the following instruction.
For the current stage of Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes, which practical detail matters next?
This stage is complete without another adjustment. Keep that result intact as you take up the next step.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I'm making Corned Beef Hash. Can you help me get the ingredients and pan ready before I turn on the stove?

Set out a large deep skillet with a lid, plus a spoon or sturdy spatula for mixing. Have 6 large potatoes, peeled and diced; 1 (12 ounce) can corned beef, cut into chunks; 1 medium onion, chopped; and 1 cup beef broth within reach.
The potatoes are diced, the onion is chopped, and I have the corned beef cut into chunks. Should the broth go in with everything else?
Yes. Put the potatoes, corned beef, chopped onion, and the full 1 cup beef broth into the large deep skillet together.
My skillet is full but everything is combined. What heat should I use?
Place the skillet over medium heat and cover it. Let the mixture simmer so the potatoes cook in the broth while the corned beef and onion heat through.
I've covered it. What am I looking for while it simmers?
Check the potatoes as it cooks. They should become soft enough to mash easily, and the broth should reduce until only a small amount of liquid remains.
Some of the broth is still visible, but the potato pieces are starting to soften. Should I uncover it?
Keep it covered while the potatoes still need softening. Once they are close to mashing consistency, watch for the liquid to become almost gone before moving on.
The potatoes crush easily against the side of the skillet now, and there is only a little liquid left.
That is the texture you want. Remove the lid and mix the hash well, breaking up the softened potatoes as you stir so the corned beef, onion, and potatoes are evenly combined.
The mixture is thick and evenly mixed. Is there anything to check before serving?
Make sure there is not a pool of broth left in the skillet and that the potatoes are soft throughout rather than firm in the center. Once those checks look right, serve the hash hot.
It is thick, with almost no liquid left, and the potatoes are fully soft. I'm ready to plate it.
Spoon the Corned Beef Hash onto plates while it is hot. The finished hash should be well mixed, with tender mashed-textured potatoes and corned beef distributed throughout.
Help me stay organized for Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. What comes first? I have 8 uncooked lasagna noodles and a pot of water ready.
Cook the 8 lasagna noodles according to the package directions, without adding salt or fat. Drain them well afterward, then lay them out so they do not stick together while you make the filling.
While the noodles cook, what should I measure for the cheese filling?
Set out 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese and 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta cheese. Drain the 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles as well.
The chiles are drained. I also see 1/2 teaspoon chili powder in my recipe notes; should that go in with the filling?

Yes. Put the Monterey Jack, ricotta, drained green chiles, and 1/2 teaspoon chili powder in a mixing bowl. Add the other ingredients called for with the cheese mixture, then stir until it is evenly combined.
My noodles are drained and pliable. How thickly should I spread the filling?
Place each noodle flat and spread the cheese mixture across one side in an even layer. Leave a small edge clear so the filling is less likely to squeeze out when you roll it.
The filling is spread, but I have not added the black beans yet. Where do they go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on all of the noodles. Aim for an even distribution so the rolls have similar filling from one to the next.
A few beans are near the edges. Should I fix that before rolling?
Move any loose beans slightly inward, especially at the narrow ends. That will make the rolls easier to close neatly.
How do I form the rolls?
Roll up each noodle jellyroll fashion, beginning at a narrow end. Keep the roll snug enough to hold together without pressing so hard that the filling escapes.
The rolls are formed. What should I check before I set them out to serve?

Check that each roll is closed, the filling is contained, and the black beans are distributed through the rolls. If any filling has spilled onto the work surface, scoop it back onto a roll or clean it away before serving.
I'm setting up for Apple Blueberry Tarts. What ingredients should I gather before I start chopping?

Set out 2 medium cooking apples, plus 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries. You'll also need 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute, 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice, whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, oil, and milk. Have two medium bowls and a fork ready.
The apples are peeled, cored, and chopped. How is the spice divided between the fruit and dough?
Keep the full 1/2 teaspoon of apple pie spice or allspice available. The directions call for 1/4 teaspoon in the apple-blueberry filling and 1/8 teaspoon in the flour mixture.
I have the fruit in one bowl. What goes in with it?
Add the blueberries, the 1 tablespoon sugar substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon of the spice to the chopped apples. Stir until the fruit is coated, then set that bowl aside while you make the dough.
What should I put in the second bowl for the crust?
Stir together 1 1/3 cups whole wheat pastry flour, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice in the second medium bowl.
The dry ingredients are mixed. Do I add the oil and milk separately?
Add the oil and milk to the flour mixture all at once. Use a fork rather than a spoon so you can bring the dough together lightly.
What texture am I looking for as I work it with the fork?
Stop once the mixture forms a cohesive dough. It should hold together when pressed, without being worked into a smooth or sticky mass; mix only as much as needed to gather the dry bits.
The dough is together. How should I portion it for the tart pans?
Divide the dough into 6 portions. Use six individual tart pans with removable bottoms, each about 3 1/2 to 4 inches across. Press one portion over the bottom and up the side of each pan.
Before I continue, what should I check on the shaped crusts?

Make sure each crust has an even layer across the bottom and reaches up the sides without thin gaps or cracks. The directions provided cover preparing the filling and shaping the crusts, so check the rest of your recipe for the filling and baking instructions before heating the oven.
I'm making Drunken Fruit Salsa for later today. Do I need to heat anything, or should I set up a bowl and fridge space?
There's no stove step here. Set out a glass bowl, a spoon for mixing, a knife and cutting board, and make room in the refrigerator for the bowl.
I have a mango and strawberries on the counter. What are the exact amounts I should prep?
Peel and finely dice 1 medium mango, and chop 3/4 cup fresh strawberries.
The mango and strawberries are cut. What remaining produce needs to be ready before I mix?
Peel and finely dice 1 kiwi. Also seed and finely chop 1 jalapeno pepper so its heat is spread evenly through the salsa.
I've got the fruit and jalapeno ready. What else goes into the glass bowl?
Add the mango, strawberries, kiwi, jalapeno, mint, and rum to the glass bowl. Stir gently enough to combine everything without crushing the fruit.
The mixture is combined, and the fruit is still in distinct pieces. Should it go straight into the refrigerator?
Yes. Cover or otherwise protect the bowl and refrigerate the salsa for 1 to 3 hours.
While it chills, do I leave it alone or check it?
Stir it once or twice during the chilling time. That redistributes the rum, mint, and juices as the fruit softens slightly.
After about an hour, it looks juicier than it did when I mixed it. Is that expected?
Yes, the fruit will release some juice as it rests. Give it a gentle stir and make sure the diced mango, kiwi, strawberries, and jalapeno are still evenly distributed.
I'm ready to serve it after chilling. What should I check at the bowl?
Stir once more, then taste a small spoonful for the balance of fruit, jalapeno, mint, and rum. Serve it while the fruit pieces are still fresh-looking and evenly coated.
Let's make Chocolate Covered Banana Pie. I want to keep the ingredients and steps organized.
Certainly. We'll organize the ingredients first and then follow the cooking cues in order.
With Chocolate Covered Banana Pie in front of me, which cue should guide the next move?
Start by preparing 1/2 cup chopped pecans; 2/3 cup butter, melted. Arrange these ingredients in its own part of the counter so the next addition stays unambiguous.
As I continue with Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Add this second group to the setup: 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips; 4 cups milk. Arrange these ingredients in its own part of the counter so the next addition stays unambiguous.
Before I handle the next part of Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, which practical detail matters next?
Press into a 9 x 13 inch pan. Pause afterward to inspect the mixture or pan.
At this point in Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, what should I prepare or inspect?
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 5 minutes. Until the cue appears, look for the recipe's intended visual cue.
At this point in Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, what belongs within reach now?
Cool. At that point, confirm the doneness.
As I continue with Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, what should I prepare or inspect?
Combine chocolate chips, 1 cup milk, and 2 cups marshmallows in a sauce pan. At that stage avoid unnecessary extra handling until the following instruction.
As I continue with Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, which practical detail matters next?
Nothing in the present texture needs reworking. Move into the following written instruction when ready.
I've got a butterflied leg of lamb ready for the cumin-and-garlic broiled lamb. Can you help me set up before I start?

Set out 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic (minced), 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, 2 tablespoons ground cumin, and 1 tablespoon dried oregano. You'll also want a large wire rack, a roasting pan, and foil.
My garlic is minced and the seasonings are measured. What do I do with the oil and spices?
Mix the olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano into a paste. Spread it over both sides of the lamb so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
The lamb is coated. Should it go straight under the broiler?
Let it stand for 1 hour, until the meat comes to room temperature. That is a good time to line the roasting pan with foil and fit the wire rack over it.
The hour is nearly up, and my lamb is fairly thick. Where should the oven rack sit?
Use the upper-middle position for a thicker piece; a thinner lamb can go on the upper rack. Preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes so it is fully hot.
The broiler has been heating for 10 minutes. How should I arrange the lamb in the pan?
Place the lamb cut side up on the wire rack over the foil-lined roasting pan. The rack keeps it elevated while the foil makes the drippings easier to manage.
It's under the broiler now. What should I watch during the first side?
Broil for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Keep an eye on spots closest to the broiler, which can color faster.
The cut side is well browned after about 8 minutes. Do I turn it now?
Yes. Turn the lamb over and broil the other side until it is well browned, about 8 minutes longer.
Both sides are browned and I'm ready to serve. Is there anything to do before slicing?
Turn off the broiler, remove the lamb from the oven, and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving. The rest gives the juices time to settle in the meat.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic

messages.content: I have the ingredients out for Corn Bread Sloppy Joes. What should I set up before I start?

Put the corn bread/muffin mix, 1 egg, and 1/3 cup milk near a bowl for the bread. Have a large skillet ready for the 2 pounds ground beef, along with a baking pan or dish called for on the corn bread package.
Should I get the corn bread going before I work on the filling?
Yes. Mix and bake the 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix according to its package directions, using the egg and milk. That lets it bake while you make the beef mixture.
While that bakes, what else needs to be beside the stove?
Set out 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1 (26 ounce) jar meatless spaghetti sauce. Also have the corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix ready to add after the meat is cooked.
The skillet is heating. How will I know the beef and onion are ready?
Cook the ground beef and chopped onion over medium heat, breaking up the meat as it cooks. When no pink meat remains and the onion has softened, drain off the excess fat.
The beef is drained and back in the skillet. Do all the remaining filling ingredients go in together?
They do. Stir in the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix until the beef is evenly coated and the additions are distributed through the skillet.
It is bubbling around the edges. Should I turn the heat up?
Bring the mixture to a full boil, stirring occasionally so the thicker sauce does not catch on the bottom. Once it reaches that boil, lower the heat.
How long should the filling stay on low heat without becoming too thick?
Simmer it uncovered for 10 minutes. It should become saucy enough to spoon over the corn bread; if it starts sticking, stir more often while keeping the heat low.
The corn bread is baked and the filling looks ready. What is the last cheese step?
Sprinkle the cheese over the hot mixture, cover the skillet, and cook for 1 minute, just until the cheese melts.
How should I serve it?
Cut the baked corn bread into portions and spoon the cheesy sloppy joe mixture over each piece. Serve while the filling is hot and the corn bread is still tender.
I'm about to start Cornbread Dressing I. Can you talk me through the prep?

Start by baking the refrigerated biscuit dough according to its package directions, making enough for 4 cups once it is crumbled. Bake the 1 (8 ounce) package corn bread mix in an 8x8 inch pan according to its package directions as well.
Should I chop the vegetables while the biscuits and cornbread bake?
Yes. Dice 1 cup of onion and 1 cup of celery, and have them ready near the stove. Also set out the margarine and chicken broth called for in the vegetable mixture.
The cornbread and biscuits are baked. Do I crumble them while they are still warm?
Let both cool first, then crumble them. The biscuits should give you about 4 cups of crumbs, and the cornbread can be crumbled from the 8x8 inch pan.
I have the breads cooling. What oven temperature will I need later?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) once the breads have cooled and been crumbled.
I'm getting the stove ingredients together. How much margarine should I have ready?
Have 1/2 cup margarine ready, along with the diced onion, diced celery, and chicken broth for the small pot.
The crumbs are in a bowl and the oven is heating. What goes into the pot?
Combine the 1 cup diced onion, 1 cup diced celery, margarine, and chicken broth in a small pot.
What should I watch for once the pot is on the heat?
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cook until the onion and celery are tender. Stir occasionally so the vegetables cook evenly and nothing catches on the bottom.
The vegetables are tender and the bread is fully crumbled. Is that the right point to continue assembling the dressing?
Yes. With the vegetables tender, the hot onion-celery mixture and the cooled, crumbled biscuits and cornbread are ready for the next assembly stage of the dressing.
I have Absolutely Awesome BBQ Sauce planned for today. What should I set up first?

Yes. Set out a saucepan, a spoon for stirring, and measuring cups. Gather 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chile sauce, 1/2 cup rum, and 1/4 cup soy sauce. The cooking directions also call for ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper.
I have the sugar, chile sauce, rum, and soy sauce measured. What about the other seasonings?
Keep 1/4 cup ketchup and 1/4 cup Worcestershire sauce nearby, along with the garlic, dry mustard, and pepper called for on your recipe card. Have everything within reach before turning on the heat.
My saucepan is ready. Should I heat it before adding anything?

Use low heat, then add the brown sugar, chile sauce, rum, soy sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper to the saucepan. Stir as they warm so the sugar begins dissolving evenly.
The sauce is mixed, but the brown sugar is still a little grainy around the edges.
Keep the heat low and stir, scraping around the sides and bottom of the pan. Once the sugar has dissolved and the sauce looks uniform, let it come to a gentle simmer.
It has reached a quiet simmer. How long does it stay there?
Simmer it for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Low heat is important here so the sauce reduces without scorching on the bottom.
About halfway through, it is darker and starting to coat my spoon.
That is a good sign of reduction. Continue the 30-minute simmer, giving it a stir whenever you see sauce collecting at the edges or settling on the bottom.
The 30 minutes are up. It is glossy and thick enough to leave a trail when I stir.
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the sauce cool. It will thicken a little more as it cools, so do not judge its final texture while it is still hot.
It has cooled down. What is the best way to hold it until dinner?
Transfer the cooled BBQ sauce to a covered container and refrigerate it until you are ready to use it. Give it a stir before serving if it has settled.
I have the ground turkey chilled. What should I set out before I start mixing the Asian Turkey Burgers?

Have a large bowl, a fork or spoon, measuring spoons, a plate for the formed patties, and a nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray ready. Measure 1 egg white, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion. Also have 1 garlic clove, minced, and 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger nearby; keep the turkey separate until the mixture is ready.
The egg white, soy sauce, bread crumbs, onion, garlic, and ginger are in front of me. Should the dry ingredients go in before the egg white?
Add everything except the turkey to the bowl and stir it together. The crumbs may look a little uneven at first, but mixing the egg white and soy sauce through them should moisten the mixture.
It is combined, though it looks fairly thick rather than smooth. Is that okay before the turkey goes in?
Yes. It should be a seasoned crumb mixture, not a smooth batter. Crumble the turkey over it, then mix only until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
What is the best way to avoid making the turkey mixture dense?
Use a light folding motion and stop as soon as you no longer see separate pockets of crumbs or seasoning. Avoid pressing or kneading it repeatedly.
The mixture is together. How should I portion the patties?
Divide the mixture into four similar portions and gently shape them into four patties. Make each one even in thickness so they cook at about the same rate.
The patties are formed. My skillet is nonstick—what should I do before adding them?
Coat the skillet with nonstick cooking spray and heat it before adding the patties. Arrange them with a little room between each one so they can cook without sticking together.
The patties are cooking and the bottoms are starting to brown. When should I turn them?
Turn them once the underside has set and releases cleanly from the skillet. Continue cooking after the turn until the centers are no longer pink.
One patty is thicker than the others. What should I check before serving?
Check the thickest patty at its center; it should be cooked through with no pink remaining. Once all four patties meet that check, transfer them from the skillet and serve while hot.
I'm making Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. My butter is softened—can you help me get organized before I mix?

Set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and have a large bowl ready. Put out 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening, 1 cup packed light brown sugar, and 1/2 cup white sugar.
I have those on the counter. What else should be measured before I start creaming them?
Have 2 eggs and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract ready for the bowl. Also gather the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, salt, oats, and raisins so they are ready when the base is mixed.
The butter, shortening, and sugars are in my large bowl. How should the mixture look before I add the eggs?

Cream the butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, and white sugar together until they are well blended. Then add the 2 eggs and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and keep mixing until the mixture is smooth.
It looks smooth and creamy now. Do the dry ingredients go in all at once?
Combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt separately, then stir that dry mixture into the sugar mixture. Mix just until you no longer see dry flour streaks.
The dough is fairly thick, and I don't see any loose flour. When do the oats and raisins go in?
This is the point to stir in the oats and raisins. Fold them through until they are distributed throughout the dough without overworking it.
The dough is ready. Should I grease my cookie sheets?
Use ungreased cookie sheets. Drop the dough by rounded teaspoonfuls, leaving space between portions so the cookies can spread as they bake.
One tray is portioned. How long should it bake?
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cookies are light and golden.
At the 10-minute mark, the edges are lightly golden but the centers still look soft. Is that okay?

Yes. Lightly golden edges are the key cue; the centers can remain soft when the tray comes out. If the cookies are not yet light and golden overall, continue checking within the 10 to 12 minute baking time.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks. What equipment should I put out before I start?
Set out a medium bowl and whisk for the marinade, a large resealable bag for the fish, and a refrigerator-safe spot for the bag. You'll also want an outdoor grill ready later.
I have the bowl, whisk, and bag. Which marinade ingredients need measuring?
Measure 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. Have 2 cloves of garlic peeled and minced as well.
The garlic is minced. Do I mix everything in the bowl before the fish goes into the bag?
Yes. Whisk the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, ginger, and minced garlic together in the medium bowl until the mixture looks combined.
The oil and soy sauce are blended, with ginger and garlic spread through it. What do I do with the bag?
Pour the marinade into the large resealable bag. Keep the opening upright while you fill it so the mixture does not spill.
The marinade is in the bag. Should the swordfish go in one at a time?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the marinade, seal it securely, and shake or turn the bag so the steaks are coated on all sides.
They're coated, and the bag is sealed. How long does it need to stay chilled?
Refrigerate the bag for at least 4 hours. Lay it on a plate or shallow dish in case of leaks, and keep it cold until you are ready to grill.
After the 4-hour marinade, what should I prepare before taking the fish outside?
Preheat the outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate. When you remove the swordfish from the bag, discard the used marinade rather than using it as a serving sauce.
The grill is heating and the grate is oiled. Is there anything useful to check right before grilling?

Make sure the steaks are still evenly coated and the grill grate is clean, hot, and lightly oiled. Then place the swordfish on the grill and cook it until it is done to your preferred serving doneness.
I'm getting ready to make Armadillo Eggs. What equipment should I have out before I start?
Set out a medium baking sheet, something to grease it with, a small knife for the peppers, and a bowl or container for the discarded jalapeno seeds and pulp.
I have the pan and knife ready. Can you help me check the ingredient amounts?
You should have 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese.
The peppers are whole and the cheese is already shredded. Should I heat the oven before I handle the jalapenos?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) so it is ready while you prepare the peppers.
The oven is heating. What do I do with the baking sheet?
Lightly grease the medium baking sheet. A thin, even coating is enough; you do not need to leave visible pools of grease on it.
My sheet is greased. How should I cut the jalapenos without splitting them apart?
Make one slit in each jalapeno, cutting only as far as needed to open it. Keep the pepper mostly intact rather than cutting it all the way through.
I can see the seeds through the slits. What needs to come out?
Remove and discard the seeds and the pale inner pulp from each pepper. Work over your discard bowl so the prepared peppers stay clear of the scraps.
A few peppers still have small seed bits clinging inside. Do they need to be completely clean?
Clear out the seeds and pulp as thoroughly as you can. It is fine to take an extra moment with the narrow ends of the peppers before moving them to the greased baking sheet.
All 24 jalapenos are slit, seeded, and on the pan. What should I keep nearby for the rest of the recipe?

Keep the 1 pound sausage, the 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and the 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese within reach. Your peppers are prepped, the baking sheet is ready, and the oven should be at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
I'm making Fruited Ice Cream. Which equipment should I get ready before I start?

Set up the ice cream maker with its freezer canister fully prepared as its manufacturer directs. Keep a large bowl or pitcher, a whisk or sturdy spoon, and measuring spoons nearby so the mixture can go straight into the canister.
I have the maker ready. Can you help me check the ingredients before I open everything?
Gather 2 (14 ounce) cans of sweetened condensed milk, 5 cups milk, 2 cups heavy cream, and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract. The method also calls for fruit and salt, so have those ready as well.
My copy has a note for 1/2 teaspoon salt, but it does not say what fruit or how much fruit to use. Is that okay?

Yes. Use the 1/2 teaspoon salt from your note. Since the fruit is not specified, choose a fruit you want in the ice cream and use the amount given on any accompanying recipe note rather than guessing from the base ingredients.
Should I mix the condensed milk with the dairy in a separate bowl, or put it directly into the canister?

You can combine everything directly in the freezer canister if it has enough room to stir without spilling. Add the sweetened condensed milk, milk, heavy cream, vanilla, salt, and fruit, then stir until the condensed milk is fully blended through.
The mixture is in the canister. What should it look like before I start the machine?

It should look evenly creamy, with no dense streaks of condensed milk at the bottom or sides. Make sure the vanilla and salt are distributed and that the fruit is dispersed rather than sitting in one clump.
It looks smooth and the fruit is mixed through. Do I need to heat or chill it first?
No heating is called for. Move on to freezing the mixture in the ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's directions for your machine.
The machine is running. How do I know whether the texture is developing normally?

Check it periodically according to the maker's guidance. The mixture should gradually thicken and become creamy; follow the machine's stated operating time and texture cues rather than adding anything extra.
What if it stays softer than I expected when the maker's cycle is done?

Use the manufacturer's directions as the guide for the completed cycle. If the mixture has thickened but is still soft, that can be normal for freshly churned ice cream; avoid trying to correct it by changing the ingredient balance.
Before I serve it, what final check should I make?

Make sure the ice cream is evenly frozen with the fruit distributed throughout, then taste a small spoonful for vanilla and sweetness. Wipe the canister rim clean and serve once the texture is where you want it.
Before I turn on the stove for Chicken and Black Bean Chili, I have a large pot, 2 tablespoons cooking oil, and the chicken ready. Should the chicken stay in 1 inch pieces?
Yes. Keep the 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces so they brown evenly. Have sea salt and 1 tablespoon chili powder nearby as well.
For the onion and bell peppers in Chicken and Black Bean Chili, use the first cut from the two raw-vegetable options we discussed earlier.
Got it—I'll use the first of those two cuts for the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper in this chili.
Yes, that's the one. I don't want to revisit the choice tonight; just help me cook the chili.
Absolutely. We'll stick with that vegetable cut and keep the cooking moving.
What else should I place beside the pot before the oil goes in?
Set out the 1/2 tablespoon ground cumin, plus ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Keep the prepared onion and both bell peppers close by, using the chosen first cut.
The 2 tablespoons of oil are warming in the large pot over medium heat. When should the chicken go in?
Once the oil is hot and fluid, add the chicken in a single layer if you can. Let it brown on all sides rather than stirring it constantly.
The chicken has color on most sides, with a few pale spots left. Should I season it before adding the vegetables?

Yes. Season the chicken with sea salt, the 1 tablespoon chili powder, the 1/2 tablespoon cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir long enough to coat the chicken and let the spices become fragrant.
The spices are coating the chicken without scorching. Are the vegetables next?
Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, all cut according to the first option you chose. Stir them through the seasoned chicken so they begin to soften evenly.
The peppers are starting to soften, and I'm planning to serve soon. What should I do with the water?
Pour in about 3 cups water. Continue cooking for 10 minutes, until about 1/2 the water has evaporated, stirring occasionally so the bottom does not catch.
After the 10 minutes, what should I check before I ladle it out?

Check that the chicken is cooked through, the vegetables are as tender as you like, and the liquid has reduced by roughly 1/2. Taste for sea salt and chili seasoning, then serve the Chicken and Black Bean Chili.
For the creamy sauce texture in Flavorful Rice Dressing 2, let's use the second option from the pair we discussed earlier.
Absolutely. I'll use the second option for the creamy sauce texture while we make Flavorful Rice Dressing 2.
Yes, that's the one. I don't want to revisit the choice tonight; please just guide me through the dressing.
Understood. Set out a large bowl, a skillet, a stirring spoon, and a greased 2-qt casserole so everything is ready when the mixture comes together.
I have 7 slices of day-old bread torn up, plus 1 cup of torn corn bread. How should I handle the bread?
Put both breads in the large bowl. Pour in 2/3 cup hot water and toss lightly, just enough to moisten the pieces without crushing them.
The bread is moistened. I have 1/2 cup thinly sliced celery ready; should I get the other vegetables beside the skillet?
Yes. Have the celery, 1/2 cup chopped onion, mushrooms, and oil within reach before you heat the skillet.
My skillet is heating with the oil. What am I looking for with the vegetables?
Add the celery, onion, and mushrooms. Sauté them until tender, stirring constantly so they soften evenly and do not catch on the pan.
The celery has softened and the onion and mushrooms are tender. Does this go straight into the bread bowl?
It does. Stir the sautéed vegetables into the moistened bread mixture until they are spread through it.
The vegetables are mixed in, and the texture is still loose enough to stir. What comes next?
Add the remaining ingredients called for in the recipe and mix well, scraping around the bowl so the bread and vegetables are evenly combined.
Everything is combined. How should I get it ready for serving without packing it down too much?
Transfer the dressing to the greased 2-qt casserole and spread it gently into an even layer rather than pressing it firmly.
It is in the casserole. What should I check before I put it on the table?

Check that the vegetables are evenly distributed, the bread is moist but not pooled with water, and the seasoning and texture suit you. Then serve Flavorful Rice Dressing 2 using the second creamy-sauce-texture option you chose.
I'm putting together a Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies mix as a gift. What should I measure out before I start?

Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need the recipe's salt and nutmeg, plus a clean 1 liter wide-mouth glass jar and a spoon or scoop for layering.
The flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg are on the counter. Do those go into the jar separately?
Combine the flour with the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg first. Mix the dry ingredients thoroughly so the leavening and spices are distributed evenly through the flour.
My flour mixture looks uniform. How should I arrange the layers so the jar looks tidy?
Put the white sugar into the clean 1 liter wide-mouth jar as the first layer. Add the flour mixture over it carefully, using a spoon if that helps keep the sides of the jar clean.
The flour layer reaches close to the top. Should I leave it loose?
Press the contents firmly into place, then seal the jar. A gentle, even press is enough; it should be compact and stable without forcing the lid.
I have the jar sealed. What should the instruction card say at the beginning?
Write: "In a large bowl: beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy." The butter should look noticeably paler and airy before the next ingredients are added.
What belongs on the card after the egg and butter instructions?
Continue with: "At low speed of an electric mixer add 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla and contents of Jar." Adding at low speed helps keep the dry mix from scattering out of the bowl.
Is there a useful check for the jar and card before I give it away?

Check that the sugar and flour mixture are packed in distinct, tidy layers, the lid is fully sealed, and the card clearly includes both the egg-and-butter instruction and the sour cream, vanilla, and jar-contents instruction.
The layers are neat, the lid is secure, and the card is attached. Anything else I should do?
That's ready to give. Keep the jar upright so the layers stay in place, and make sure the card remains attached for the person preparing the cookies.
I'm ready to make English Walnut Pie. Should I heat the oven before I start mixing?
