Wait for the alert during the knead cycle. When it sounds, add the sunflower seeds to the pan.
I don't want to miss that alert. What should I watch for while it runs?
Keep the machine nearby and listen for its add-in alert during kneading. No earlier addition is needed; the recipe specifically calls for the sunflower seeds at that alert.
Once I add them, do I need to change the cycle?
No. Add the sunflower seeds when prompted and let the selected basic white cycle continue.
Can you give me a quick check that everything is set correctly?

The pan should contain 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour, loaded in the manufacturer-recommended order. The machine should be running on the basic white cycle, with the sunflower seeds held back until the knead-cycle alert.
That's clear. I'll wait for the alert before adding the seeds.
Perfect—add the sunflower seeds when the alert sounds, then allow the bread machine to finish the basic white cycle.
I'm cooking Adriennes Tom Ka Gai tonight. I have a large saucepan ready—what should I prep before turning on the heat?

Measure 2 teaspoons peanut oil, thinly slice 2 cloves garlic, grate 2 tablespoons fresh ginger root, and chop 1/4 cup lemon grass. Also have the red pepper, coriander, cumin, chicken, onion, and bok choy ready for their later additions.
The garlic, ginger, and lemon grass are cut. Should the bok choy be prepared now too?
Yes. Finish preparing the bok choy so it can go into the saucepan after the chicken and onion. Keep the chicken and onion ready as a separate next addition.
Everything is portioned, including the 1/4 cup of chopped lemon grass. I'm ready to start.
Set the large saucepan over medium heat and heat the 2 teaspoons of peanut oil.
The oil is heating in the saucepan. What goes in once it is ready?
Add the sliced garlic, grated ginger, chopped lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Stir them in and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
After those aromatics have cooked for 2 minutes, should I add the chicken and onion together?
Yes, stir in the chicken and onion together. Keep stirring until the chicken is white and the onion is translucent, which should take 5 minutes.
The chicken is turning white, but the onion still looks opaque. Do I move on yet?
Continue cooking and stirring until the onion is translucent as well. Use that visual cue along with the 5-minute cooking time before adding the bok choy.
The chicken is white and the onion is translucent now. When should the bok choy go in?
Stir in the bok choy now. Cook until it begins to wilt, allowing 5 to 10 minutes.
The bok choy has started to wilt. Is the cooking step complete?
Yes. Once the bok choy begins to wilt, the recipe's cooking sequence is complete and the Tom Ka Gai is ready to serve.
I'm making Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake in a 9-inch springform pan. What should I gather before I start?

Set out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup margarine to melt, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream. Have the 9-inch springform pan ready; a pie plate also works.
How many cookies do I crush for the crust?
Crush half the cookies—about 20—into fine crumbs. Save the remaining cookies whole for the edge of the pan.
My margarine is melted and the crumbs are ready. How should the base look in the pan?
Mix the crumbs with the melted 1/4 cup margarine until they are evenly moistened, then press them firmly across the bottom of the pan. Aim for an even layer without loose, dry patches.
Should I place the whole cookies before adding the fudge?
Yes. Stand the reserved cookies upright around the inside edge of the pan, placing them close together so they form a neat border.
I have the cookie border in place. How much hot fudge goes over the crust?
Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crumb crust. Keep it inside the cookie border and use a gentle touch so the crumb layer stays intact.
There is still fudge left from the 1 cup. Do I use it all at this point?
No. Use only 3/4 cup for this layer. Leave the remaining fudge aside, and keep the 2 quarts of vanilla ice cream frozen until you are ready for the next assembly stage.
What should I do once the fudge layer is smooth?
Place the pan in the freezer for 15 minutes. The fudge should feel set enough that it will not smear easily when you continue assembling the cake.
How can I tell whether the crust and cookie wall are holding together after chilling?
Check that the crumb base is firm, the upright cookies are still standing, and the fudge layer is no longer runny. If those pieces are stable, the pan is ready for the ice-cream portion of the cake.
When I serve it later, what should I check before cutting?
Make sure the cake is firm enough to slice cleanly, then release the springform ring carefully. Cut with a sturdy knife, wiping it between slices if the ice cream begins to soften.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake

messages.content: I have a 1 (3 1/2)-pound broiler-fryer chicken cut up and 1 pound of new potatoes ready. What should I set beside the stove for Dilly Chicken and Potatoes?
Set out a large skillet, a spoon or spatula, and a plate for the browned pieces. Measure 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 1 cup half-and-half cream, and have salt and pepper available.
The potatoes are cut into chunks. Does the chicken need any more preparation before it goes into the skillet?
No further preparation is specified. Keep the chicken cut up and the potatoes in chunks, then you can start browning them together.
How hot should the skillet be, and how long should I brown everything?
Heat the large skillet over medium heat, add the 2 tablespoons of oil, and brown the chicken and potatoes for 10-15 minutes.
The chicken and potatoes have browned. Should I leave them in the pan while I make the creamy mixture?
Remove both the chicken and potatoes from the skillet and set them aside. Leave the pan with its drippings for the next step.
How much of the drippings should remain?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the drippings. That remaining amount will form the base for the cream mixture.
I have 1 tablespoon left in the skillet. What goes in next?
Add the 1 cup of half-and-half cream to the drippings, then season with salt and pepper and stir to mix.
What should I look for while I stir the cream into the drippings?
Stir until the cream and drippings are combined. Keep the heat at a level that lets you mix the sauce without scorching it.
Once the mixture is combined, where do the chicken and potatoes go?
Return the chicken and potatoes to the skillet and coat them with the cream mixture. Give the dish a final taste and check that the pieces are arranged securely before serving.
I have the ingredients for Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles out. Where should I begin?
Certainly. We'll organize the ingredients first and then follow the cooking cues in order.
With Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles in front of me, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Put 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves; 1 (10 ounce) can refrigerated large crescent roll dough within reach before you begin the active step.
As I continue with Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles, which cue should guide the next move?
Prepare 8 ounces Brie cheese; 1 bunch fresh spinach, rinsed and stems removed. Arrange these ingredients in its own part of the counter until the recipe calls for it.
With Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles in front of me, which cue should guide the next move?
Saute chicken breasts until no longer pink, and juices run clear; set aside. Take a moment afterward to make sure the stage looks even.
For the current stage of Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles, what belongs within reach now?
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). During this part, watch the texture closely.
Before I handle the next part of Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles, what belongs within reach now?
Unroll 4 large crescent rolls. Before moving on, check the texture against the recipe.
Before I handle the next part of Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles, which cue should guide the next move?
Layer each with 3 thin slices brie, 3 leaves spinach and 1 slice prosciutto. From there leave the result undisturbed while you clear the immediate work area.
At this point in Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Nothing in the present texture needs reworking. Let the recipe's next direction determine what happens now.
I'm making Cucumber Sandwiches. I have the counter free—what should I set out?
Gather 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
Should I peel the cucumbers before slicing them?
Peel them if you wish, then thinly slice both cucumbers. The recipe works either way on the peeling.
The cucumbers are sliced. How do I make the spread?
In a bowl, combine the cream cheese spread with the 2 teaspoons of ranch salad dressing mix until evenly blended.
The mixture is smooth. Do I spread it on every slice of bread?
Yes. Spread the cream cheese mixture on one side of each of the 12 pumpernickel rye slices.
All the bread is covered. Which slices get the cucumber?
Arrange the thin cucumber slices on six slices of bread, covering the spread without piling them too heavily.
The cucumber is in place. Should I add anything before closing the sandwiches?
No additional ingredient is needed. Top the cucumber-covered slices with the remaining bread, spread-side facing inward.
How can I check that they're assembled neatly?
Make sure each sandwich has cucumber between two bread slices and that the edges line up. Press gently so the layers hold together.
They're assembled. Can I serve the Cucumber Sandwiches now?
Yes, they're ready to serve. If desired, tidy the edges before placing the sandwiches on a serving plate.
I have the bowl and baking sheets ready for Grandmas Gingersnaps. What should I do before mixing?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, measure 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses.
What else should I measure before I start the dough?
Set out the dry ingredients as well: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon ground ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Keep the wet ingredients and dry mixture separate for now.
The oven is heating, and everything is measured. How do I begin the mixture?
In a medium bowl, cream the 3/4 cup margarine with 1 cup white sugar until the mixture is smooth.
The margarine and sugar look smooth. What goes in next?
Beat in 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses until they are well blended into the creamed mixture.
The wet mixture is blended. How should I add the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt, then stir that mixture into the molasses mixture until it forms a dough.
The dough has come together. What size should I make the cookies?
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each ball in the remaining sugar.
The dough balls are coated. How should I arrange them on the pans?
Place the balls 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets so they have room as they bake.
The sheets are loaded. What should I verify before putting them in the oven?

Confirm that the oven is at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and that the cookies are spaced 2 inches apart on ungreased sheets. The directions provided do not include a baking time, so use the timing from your recipe card and check the cookies for doneness before serving.
For the BBQ Chicken Wings, use the first sauce-mixing version we discussed earlier.
Absolutely. I'll use that first sauce version for tonight's wings and keep the rest of the preparation on track.
Yes, that's the one. I don't want to revisit the choice; please guide me through the wings.
You've got it. We'll stick with that sauce approach for this batch.
I'm clearing space by the bowl. Which measured ingredients should I keep within reach?

Set out 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce, 1 cup oyster sauce, 1/4 cup soy sauce, and 1/4 cup ketchup. Keep 2 tablespoons garlic powder nearby as well, along with the gin, liquid smoke, and sugar called for in the mixing directions.
The sauces are lined up. Do the garlic powder and the other flavorings go into the same bowl?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the teriyaki sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar, using the first sauce-mixing version you chose.
The sauce is mixed. What do I do with the chicken wings before I start the grill?
Put the wings into the bowl and coat them in the marinade. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it for 8 hours or overnight.
The wings have finished marinating. What should I prepare at the grill?
Preheat the grill over low heat, then lightly oil the grill grate so the wings are less likely to stick.
Once the wings go on, how can I keep their texture from getting too dark or dry?
Arrange the wings on the low-heat grill and watch their browning as they cook. Use doneness as the guide rather than adding an unlisted shortcut or increasing the heat.
There is marinade left in the bowl after I put the wings on the grill. Can that stay for serving?
Discard the marinade after the wings are on the grill; do not use the leftover marinade as a serving sauce.
When I'm ready to plate them, what should I look over one last time?
Before serving, check that the wings are done, then look over their taste, texture, and placement on the platter.
I'm making Coconut Ambrosia Salad and want to keep it simple. The directions mention a couple of items that are not in my ingredient list—can you help me get organized before I mix anything?

This is a chilled, no-cook salad. The listed ingredients are 1 (11 ounce) can mandarin oranges, drained; 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, drained; 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed; and 2 cups shredded coconut. The mixing directions also call for marshmallows and milk, but no amounts are provided there, so confirm those amounts from your recipe source before combining everything. You will also need cherries for the garnish.
Why is it important to drain both cans well?

Draining the mandarin oranges and crushed pineapple keeps excess juice from loosening the whipped topping. Let the fruit sit in a colander for a few minutes, then give it a gentle shake so it is drained without crushing the orange segments.
I checked the source and have the marshmallows and milk ready in the amounts it specifies. What should be on the counter beside my large bowl?

Set out the drained oranges and pineapple, the thawed 3 1/2 cups of whipped topping, and 2 cups of shredded coconut, along with the marshmallows and milk called for in your directions. A flexible spatula or large spoon will make it easier to mix without breaking up the fruit.
The fruit is drained and the whipped topping is soft. Should I do anything else before it all goes into the bowl?
Make sure there is no pooled juice under the fruit and that the whipped topping is thawed enough to scoop smoothly. Once those are ready, there is no heating or separate cooking step needed.
Everything is measured and ready. How do I combine it?

Put the oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows, and milk into the large bowl. Mix them together well, using gentle turns of the spatula so the fruit is evenly distributed and the whipped topping coats the other ingredients.
I've mixed it. What tells me it is blended enough to refrigerate?

It is ready for the refrigerator when the coconut and marshmallows are spread throughout the mixture, the fruit is coated with whipped topping, and there are no obvious pockets of unmixed coconut or milk. Chill it for 1 hour before serving.
Should the cherries go in before the bowl is chilled?
Hold the cherries until serving. You can cover the bowl while it chills to keep the salad protected in the refrigerator, then use the cherries as the final garnish.
The 1 hour chill is nearly finished. What should I check before putting it on the table?
Make sure the salad is thoroughly chilled and still has a fluffy, cohesive texture rather than separated liquid around the edges. Garnish with cherries, then serve the Coconut Ambrosia Salad cold.
Let's make Chocolate Madeleines. I want to keep the ingredients and steps organized.
Here, we'll separate the setup from the active cooking so each stage stays clear.
For the current stage of Chocolate Madeleines, which practical detail matters next?
Start by preparing 1/2 teaspoon baking powder; 1 pinch salt. Arrange these ingredients separate and verify the amounts before combining anything.
As I continue with Chocolate Madeleines, which practical detail matters next?
The next ingredients to stage are 2 ounces butter; 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract. Arrange these ingredients separate and verify the amounts before combining anything.
Before I handle the next part of Chocolate Madeleines, what should I pay attention to before proceeding?
