Set out 1/2 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced, along with garlic powder to taste. Have paper towels ready as well, since the browned chicken will need a place to drain.
The chicken is cut up already. Which pan and main ingredients should be beside the stove?
Use a large Dutch oven. Keep 2 tablespoons olive oil ready, plus the 1 (4 pound) chicken, cut into pieces, and the garlic powder.
Everything is arranged, and the Dutch oven is on the burner. How do I start?
Heat the olive oil in the large Dutch oven over medium heat. Let the oil warm before adding the chicken.
The oil is hot and moving easily across the bottom. Is this when I season the chicken?
Yes. Sprinkle the chicken with garlic powder, then brown the pieces on both sides in the Dutch oven.
The pieces have color on both sides. What should I do with them while I deal with the fat in the pan?
Remove the browned chicken to paper towels. That will hold the pieces while you clear the excess fat from the Dutch oven.
The chicken is draining, and there is a noticeable layer of fat left behind. What is the cleanup move here?
Spoon off the chicken fat, then return the pan to the stove for the next part of the recipe.
Before serving, I'm still not choosing between the two brittle-topping looks—just keeping the side mark ahead of the two-corner arrangement.

That order remains unchanged: the small uneven brittle pieces in one narrow side mark are the first possibility, and the coarse pieces in two compact opposite-corner clusters are the second. You can leave the decision open until plating.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken and Herbs in White Wine

messages.content: I have a skillet ready. What do I need for Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad, and where should I begin?

Gather 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided; 2 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves; 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning; and 2 cloves garlic, crushed. Warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Should I season the chicken while the oil is heating?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken with the 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning while the skillet heats.
The oil is hot and the chicken is seasoned. What goes into the skillet?
Place the seasoned chicken in the hot oil. Then stir in the 2 cloves of crushed garlic.
The garlic is in. How long should I leave the chicken on this side?
Cook it for 5 minutes on the first side over the medium heat specified in the recipe.
Five minutes have passed, and the underside is browned. Should I turn it now?
Turn the chicken and cook the second side for another 5 minutes.
What should I use to tell whether it is done besides the timer?
Check the thickest part as it finishes. The recipe's doneness check is that the juices should run clear.
The second side has had 5 minutes, but I want to verify before serving.
Check the chicken now. If the juices run clear, it has reached the recipe's stated doneness; if not, continue cooking until they do.
Once the juices run clear, is the cooking step complete?
Yes. When the juices run clear, the chicken is cooked according to the recipe and is ready for the salad.
For Cinnamon Bread I, I'm still undecided about how I want the sauce detail to look when it is served.

You could keep two serving looks in mind: first, place the sauce in two small pools on opposite sides of the bowl. Second, drizzle it in two thin lines across the top and leave a little extra sauce alongside.
Please leave those two Cinnamon Bread I ideas in that first-then-second order. I'll wait until I see the finished bread before deciding.
Absolutely. They can stay as two separate serving possibilities while you make the loaf.
I have a 9x5-inch loaf pan ready. Which dry ingredients should I measure before I start mixing?
Set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. Turn the oven on to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can preheat while you work.
The oven is heating. Should I prepare the pan before the batter comes together?
Yes—grease one 9x5-inch loaf pan now, making sure the bottom and corners are coated so the loaf releases cleanly.
What else goes into the large mixing bowl with those dry ingredients?

Measure the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla into a large mixing bowl. Use the amounts on your recipe card for the ingredients whose quantities are not listed here.
Once everything is in the bowl, what should the mixing look like so I do not overwork it?
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes. Keep the bowl steady and scrape down the sides if dry flour is clinging there, so the batter comes together evenly.
Before I move the batter toward the pan, what should I check?

Check that the oven is holding at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), the 9x5-inch pan is greased, and the batter has been beaten for the full 3 minutes. The directions you have stop after mixing, so follow the rest of your recipe card for transferring and baking it.
I'll keep the sauce decision for serving rather than mixing it into the bread. Can you repeat the two looks without choosing one?
Certainly: first, two small pools of sauce on opposite sides of the bowl. Second, two thin sauce lines across the top, with extra sauce nearby. Both remain open options.
That works. Keep them in that order; I am not settling on either presentation yet.
They remain in first-then-second order, with no presentation choice made yet.
I have the ingredients for Almond Apricot Bread out. Where should I begin?
Of course. We'll keep the work area orderly and use the recipe's texture and timing cues as we go.
As I continue with Almond Apricot Bread, which practical detail matters next?
Measure this first group: 1/2 cup packed brown sugar; 3 teaspoons baking powder. Leave these items clearly organized while you finish the remaining setup.
Before I handle the next part of Almond Apricot Bread, how do I tell that this part is settled?
Add this second group to the setup: 1 teaspoon salt; 2 (4 ounce) jars apricot baby food, divided. Leave these items clearly organized while you finish the remaining setup.
For the current stage of Almond Apricot Bread, what belongs within reach now?
In another bowl, beat the egg, milk, oil, extract and remaining baby food. At the end of this move to make sure the stage looks even.
As I continue with Almond Apricot Bread, which cue should guide the next move?
Stir into dry ingredients just until moistened. Until the cue appears, avoid making an unrelated adjustment.
At this point in Almond Apricot Bread, what belongs within reach now?
Fold in almonds and apricots. At that point, confirm the doneness.
For the current stage of Almond Apricot Bread, which practical detail matters next?
Pour into a greased 9-in loaf pan. Once it is complete leave the result undisturbed until the following instruction.
As I continue with Almond Apricot Bread, what should I pay attention to before proceeding?
Nothing in the present texture needs reworking. Proceed without adding an unlisted operation.
Before I start Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa, could you lay out two possible ways to handle the cilantro? I want to see both before deciding.

Certainly. First, tear the cilantro into broad pieces and tuck it into a narrow strip along one side of the tacos. Second, chop it finely, fold half into the warm filling, and scatter the rest over the tacos at the end.
Please keep those in that first-then-second order for now. I want to see how the tacos come together before I choose.
I'll keep both options in that order while we work, without treating either one as your final call.
My grill is still cold. What should I set out before I start heating it?
Set out your grill tools and a medium bowl for the salsa, then preheat the grill for high heat. Keep the bowl away from the grill so the salsa stays crisp while you cook.
I'm arranging the salsa ingredients beside the bowl. What goes in front?
Put 1 cup corn, 1/2 cup diced red onion, 1 cup peeled, chopped jicama, and 1/2 cup diced red bell pepper within easy reach of the medium bowl.
I have those measured. Where should I place the cilantro, lime, and seasonings so I do not mix things too early?

Keep the cilantro and the lime beside the salsa bowl, since the lime juice and zest are added after the vegetables are mixed. Put cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt near a separate small bowl.
The grill is heating up. What should I look for before I turn back to the salsa?
Let it fully preheat on high heat. Meanwhile, keep the chopped vegetables covered or shaded from the grill's heat so they remain crunchy.
The salsa bowl is ready. How should I combine the vegetables?
In the medium bowl, mix together the corn, red onion, jicama, red bell pepper, and cilantro. Toss gently enough to keep the jicama and bell pepper pieces intact.
The vegetables are mixed and still crisp. What brightens the salsa next?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest, coating the mixture evenly. Taste the balance after mixing rather than adding anything extra right away.
I'm nearly ready to serve. What is the final seasoning prep I should complete?

In the small bowl, combine the cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt. Before serving, check the salsa for crunch and brightness, then use whichever of the two cilantro treatments you decide suits this batch.

source_seed.recipe_title: Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa

messages.content: I'm making Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme. I have a large bowl ready for the marinade—what should I measure into it?

Measure 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed. Your recipe note also calls for 1/2 teaspoon Hungarian sweet paprika. Whisk the mixture smooth in the large bowl.
The yogurt mixture is smooth, with the celery seed and paprika evenly distributed. Should the chicken go straight into this bowl?
Yes. Add the chicken to the mixture and turn each piece so all sides are coated.
A few spots on the chicken are still bare after turning it. Do I need more marinade?
No extra marinade is needed. Turn the pieces once more and press them gently into the mixture so the surface is covered.
The chicken is coated. How should I hold it before baking tomorrow?
Cover the bowl and marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator. Keep it chilled for the entire marinating time.
It has marinated overnight, and I have crumbs ready on a plate. What should I do as I take the chicken out?
Remove each piece from the marinade, letting excess mixture drip back into the bowl briefly. Then coat each piece with crumbs, pressing lightly so the crumbs adhere.
The crumbs are sticking, but I do not want the coating to fall off while it bakes. Where should I put the pieces?
Arrange the crumb-coated chicken in a shallow baking pan, leaving a little space between pieces so the coating can brown evenly.
The chicken is in the shallow pan. The note I have does not show a baking temperature or time—what should I watch for?

Use the temperature and timing from the complete recipe card if you have them. For safety, bake until the thickest part of each chicken breast reaches 165°F, checking with an instant-read thermometer without touching the pan.
Before I serve it, what is the final check?
Confirm that the chicken has reached 165°F in the center and that the crumb coating is set and lightly browned. Let the pieces rest briefly in the pan before transferring them to plates.
I'm making Caraway Rye Muffins and have a muffin tin ready. What should I measure before I start mixing?
Set out 1 cup rye flour, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup sugar, and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder. You'll also need the recipe's salt, caraway seeds, cheese, egg, milk, and oil.
The dry ingredients are on the counter. Should I prepare the muffin cups before the batter?
Yes—grease the muffin cups or line them with paper liners now, so the batter can go straight in once it is mixed.
I have a large bowl. What goes into it first?
Combine both flours with the sugar, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds in the large bowl. Stir until the dry ingredients look evenly distributed.
The caraway is mixed through, with no obvious baking-powder clumps. Where does the cheese fit in?
Stir the cheese into the dry mixture, spreading it through rather than leaving it gathered in one spot.
I'm ready to add the liquids. Should the egg, milk, and oil be mixed separately?
Combine the egg, milk, and oil together, then pour them into the bowl of dry ingredients and cheese.
How much should I stir once the wet mixture is in? Rye batter can look a little rough.
Stir only until the ingredients are moistened. A slightly uneven-looking batter is preferable to overmixing; stop once you no longer see dry flour.
The batter is thick but moist, and the lined tin is beside me. How full should each cup be?
Fill each greased or paper-lined muffin cup about two-thirds full. Leaving that space gives the batter room to rise.
All the cups are filled about two-thirds full. Is there anything useful to check before they go into the oven?

Make sure the portions are reasonably even and that the tops are not smeared across the pan. Then bake according to the recipe's baking directions, since the provided steps do not specify an oven temperature or baking time.
I'm making Fresh Apple Salsa, and one small herb detail could go in either of two directions. I want to consider both before deciding.

Either approach can work here. First: cut the tender lower herb pieces into tiny, uneven bits and add them to the early mixture. Second: cut only the softest lower herb pieces into tiny bits, keeping the upper green pieces separate.
Keep those two Fresh Apple Salsa options in that order for my notes. I'll wait to decide until I see how the preparation feels.
Understood—I'll leave the herb choice open for now and won't treat either option as selected while we prepare the salsa.
I'm at the cutting board. Which ingredients should I measure and prep before using the bowl?
Set out 2 tart apples, cored and cubed, along with 4 tablespoons lime juice. Also prepare 1 fresh jalapeno pepper, seeded and sliced, and 1 fresh Anaheim chile, seeded and sliced.
The apples and chiles are ready. Should the lime juice go on the apples before I add anything spicy?
Yes. In a large bowl, stir the cubed apples together with the 4 tablespoons of lime juice before adding the peppers.
The apples are coated with lime juice. What should I add next, and should I stir them in right away?
Stir in the seeded, sliced jalapeno and Anaheim chile now, mixing them through the apples and lime juice.
I also have onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt ready beside the bowl. Do those go in together?
Add the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt to the bowl, then work them through the apple-and-chile mixture.
Everything listed is in the bowl. How do I bring the salsa together without leaving pockets of seasoning?
Mix thoroughly so the apples, chiles, onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt are distributed throughout.
It's mixed. What should I look at before I put out the Fresh Apple Salsa?
Check the taste and texture, and make sure the mixture is evenly combined before serving.
I still haven't chosen between the two herb treatments. Can I leave that decision open for this batch?

Yes. Keep the first version—tiny uneven pieces from the tender lower herb sections added early—and the second version—tiny pieces from only the softest lower sections with the upper green pieces separate—in that order as nonbinding options.
I'm making Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken tonight. Can you help me set up the glaze before I handle the chicken?
Set out a medium bowl, a whisk or spoon, and 1/2 cup ketchup. You'll also need 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum.
I have the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum measured. What goes into the bowl with them?

Combine all of those in the medium bowl with the mustard and garlic called for in the recipe. If you are using the Dijon-style mustard noted with the recipe, measure 2 tablespoons. Stir until the glaze looks evenly blended.
Should I season the glaze before it touches the chicken?
Yes. Add salt and pepper to taste, then mix well. The glaze should be smooth enough to brush over the chicken without separate streaks of molasses or ketchup.
The glaze is mixed. I have chicken pieces and a 9x13 inch baking dish ready—how should I prepare the dish?
Lightly oil the 9x13 inch baking dish and arrange the chicken pieces in it. Brush both sides of the chicken with the prepared glaze.
Do I use all of the glaze on the chicken now?
Use about 1/2 of the glaze for this coating. Keep the remaining half separate rather than pouring it over the raw chicken.
The chicken is coated on both sides and the rest of the glaze is still in the bowl. What happens before cooking?
Cover the baking dish and refrigerate the chicken to marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight if that suits your schedule. Refrigerate the remaining glaze as well.
What should I check when I take the dish out after marinating?

Make sure the chicken is still arranged in the lightly oiled dish and has an even glaze coating. The marinating instructions end there, so check the complete recipe for its baking temperature and cooking time before proceeding.
Once I have the cooking directions, is there anything important to keep in mind for serving?

Cook the chicken according to the full recipe directions and confirm it is fully cooked before serving. The reserved glaze should stay refrigerated until the recipe tells you how to use it; do not treat glaze that contacted raw chicken as a serving sauce.
I'm making Banana Orange Bars. What should I set out before mixing?

Measure 2 cups mashed ripe bananas, 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 cup vegetable oil, and 4 eggs. You'll also need a mixing bowl and a greased 15-in. baking pan; keep the dry ingredients separate for the moment.
The bananas are mashed, and I've measured the sugar and oil. Should the eggs go in with them?
Yes. Put the bananas, sugar, oil, and 4 eggs in the mixing bowl, then beat everything until well blended.
How do I know that mixture is ready for the dry ingredients?
It's ready when the bananas, sugar, oil, and eggs are evenly combined. Then combine the dry ingredients separately and fold them into the banana mixture until well mixed.
I've folded in the dry ingredients. The batter looks uniform—what comes next?
Follow the next recipe direction: spread over bars. Work gently so the mixture stays evenly distributed.
I've spread it as directed. Which pan should I use?
Pour the mixture into a greased 15-in. baking pan.
Should I put the pan in the oven now?

The instructions provided end with pouring the mixture into the greased pan; they do not include an oven temperature or baking time, so use the remaining directions from your full recipe before baking.
The batter is in the pan. Is there anything else from this recipe section to check?

Confirm that the mixture is spread evenly in the greased 15-in. baking pan and that all four eggs and the measured ingredients were incorporated. No serving or doneness details are included in the directions provided.
All four eggs went in, and the pan is ready. What should I do after baking?
Use the recipe's remaining baking and serving directions for the pan, since this excerpt does not specify the bake time, temperature, cooling instructions, or serving steps.
I'm making Dutch Cream Waffles. Which bowls and tools should I set out before separating the eggs?

Set out a large mixing bowl for the flour and salt, a small mixing bowl for the yolks and cream, and another small bowl for the whites. Have beaters ready; they will need to be clean when you whip the whites.
I've separated the eggs. How should I keep the portions organized?
Keep the 3 egg yolks in the small bowl and the 3 egg whites in their own bowl. Make sure no yolk has gotten into the whites, since the whites need to whip to stiff peaks later.
What ingredients should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1 cup heavy whipping cream. Keep the cream beside the yolks so it is ready to add while the mixer runs.
The flour and salt are in the large bowl. Should I do anything else to the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour and salt in the large mixing bowl so the salt is evenly distributed. You can use a whisk or stir them together briefly.
My yolks are in the small bowl and the cream is measured. What speed should the mixer be on?
Beat the egg yolks on low speed while adding the cream. Once the cream is incorporated, continue beating for 1 minute.
After that minute, the yolk and cream mixture looks uniform. How do I bring it into the flour?
Add the yolk-and-cream mixture to the flour mixture. Combine on low speed at first, then beat on medium-high until the batter is smooth.
The batter is smooth, but I have not touched the egg whites yet. What is the right check before whipping them?
Use the other small mixing bowl and clean beaters for the 3 egg whites. Any grease or yolk residue can keep them from reaching the proper volume.
The beaters are clean and the whites are ready. What texture am I looking for?
Beat the egg whites on high until stiff peaks form. When you lift the beaters, the peaks should stand upright rather than folding over.
The whites have stiff peaks and the yolk batter is smooth. Is there a final thing to confirm before cooking?

Check that the flour mixture is smooth and that the whites still hold stiff peaks. The directions provided cover the batter preparation but do not specify when to combine the whites or give waffle-iron heating and cooking directions, so verify those steps on the complete recipe before proceeding.
I'm getting ready to make Cabbage Kielbasa Supper. What equipment and ingredients should I have nearby?
Set out a 5-qt. slow cooker, 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2-inch cubes, 1 medium chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, broth, and the sausage.
The potatoes and onion are prepped. Should I add the cabbage to the slow cooker before seasoning?
Yes. Combine the cabbage, potatoes, onion, salt, and pepper in the slow cooker. Stir them together so the seasoning is distributed before adding the liquid.
How much broth goes in, and do I add it before the sausage?
Pour the broth over all of the vegetables and seasonings. Then place the sausage on top rather than mixing it underneath.
The slow cooker looks very full. Is that a problem?
That is expected at this point. The slow cooker will be full, but the cabbage will cook down as the supper cooks.
Everything is loaded. What setting and cooking time should I use?
Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 8-9 hours.
If I check it before the timer is done, what signs should I look for?
Check whether the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through. Those are the recipe's doneness checks, so use them along with the 8-9-hour timing.
The cabbage has reduced and the potatoes are nearly tender. Should I leave the lid on?
Keep it covered and continue cooking on low until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through. Avoid changing the cooking setting while it finishes.
The vegetables are tender and the sausage is hot. Can I serve the supper now?
Yes. Once those doneness checks are met, turn off the slow cooker and serve the cabbage, potatoes, onion, and sausage while hot.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks. Before I start, can you help me set up the marinade without making extra components?

Set out a medium bowl, whisk, large resealable bag, and the swordfish steaks. For the marinade, measure 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. The written instruction also calls for garlic, though no amount is provided in the ingredient list, so check your recipe source before adding it.
The bowl and bag are ready. Should the swordfish go into the bag first, or should I mix the liquid separately?
Mix the marinade separately. Whisk the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, grated ginger, and the garlic called for by the instruction in the medium bowl until the oil and soy sauce are well combined.
What should the mixture look like when it has been whisked enough?
It should look evenly mixed, with the ginger dispersed through the liquid. Some separation of the oil can happen if it sits, so give it another whisk just before transferring it.
I have a smooth-looking marinade. How do I transfer it without making a mess?
Open the large resealable bag wide in a bowl or measuring cup for support, then pour the marinade into the bag. Keeping the bag supported makes it easier to add the fish cleanly.
The marinade is in the bag. I'm about to add the swordfish steaks—anything to watch for?
Place the swordfish steaks in the bag with the marinade, press out excess air, and seal it securely. Gently shake and turn the bag so the mixture coats all sides of the steaks.
They're coated. Can I leave the bag on the counter while I get the rest of dinner organized?

Refrigerate it rather than leaving it out. Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the steaks marinate for at least 4 hours; laying the bag flat helps keep the fish in contact with the marinade.
Should I do anything during those 4 hours?
If convenient, turn the sealed bag once or twice so the marinade continues to coat the fish evenly. Keep it refrigerated the whole time and make sure the bag remains tightly sealed.
The recipe stops after marinating. What is the useful check when I take the swordfish out later?

Confirm that the steaks are evenly coated and that the bag has stayed sealed. This recipe provides the marinade and the minimum 4-hour chilling time, but it does not include a cooking method or cooking time, so use a separate reliable swordfish-cooking instruction before serving.
I'm making California Chicken tonight. Can you keep me on track with the listed ingredients and cooking order?
Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also want a skillet and a way to check the chicken as it cooks.
The chicken is ready. Should I heat the oven before I start the pan?
Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) before working at the stove. The written cooking steps focus on the skillet, so have that heating while the oven comes up to temperature.
I'm at the skillet. How should I use the oil without the chicken sticking?
Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet over a moderate heat, then add the chicken. Let the pan heat enough for the oil to loosen and coat the surface before the chicken goes in.
The instructions say to add chicken and onion, but my ingredient list has onion powder. What should go into the pan?

The instruction reads, "Warm oil in skillet and add chicken and onion," while the ingredient list specifies 1/2 teaspoon onion powder. Using the listed ingredients, add the chicken and onion powder to the warm oil.
The chicken is sizzling now. What should I look for while it browns?
Keep the pieces in a single layer and watch for an even browned surface. Adjust the heat if the pan is scorching before the chicken has time to brown, and turn the breasts as needed for even color.
One side is browned, but the centers still look underdone. How long should I continue?
Cook for 15 minutes or until the chicken is browned and just about done, as the recipe directs. Use the color and firmness of the thickest part as your check rather than relying on browning alone.
The chicken has browned and feels firmer. What seasoning goes on at the end?
Add the 1 pinch salt, then add pepper to taste. Toss or turn the chicken briefly so the seasoning reaches both sides.
Before I plate it, is there anything important to check?
Make sure the chicken is cooked through at its thickest point, then taste a small piece and adjust pepper if needed. Once it is fully cooked and seasoned, it is ready to serve.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana with 4 pounds of dark-meat chicken. What should I set up before the skillet goes on?

Have a large skillet ready, along with 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, the chicken, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, and poultry seasoning for the flour. Use a shallow bowl or plate for the seasoned flour, and keep a clean plate nearby for the browned chicken.
Should the garlic be mixed into the flour with the poultry seasoning?
No. Season the flour with the poultry seasoning, but keep the crushed garlic separate. Half of the garlic goes into the hot oil before the chicken is added.
The flour is seasoned and the chicken is ready to dredge. What am I looking for when I heat the skillet?
Warm the vegetable oil in the large skillet until it moves easily across the pan. Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic and let it become fragrant without letting it darken.
The garlic smells good and is still pale. Can I coat the chicken now?
Yes. Dredge the chicken pieces in the seasoned flour, shaking off excess so the coating is light rather than clumpy. Put the pieces into the skillet with some space between them.
My skillet will not hold all 4 pounds in a single layer. Is it better to crowd it or work in batches?
Work in batches. A single layer gives the flour-coated chicken room to brown instead of steam, and you can return the browned pieces to the clean plate as you go.
One piece is browning faster around the edges than the rest. Should I turn it?
Turn it when the underside has developed a golden-brown crust. Adjust the heat if the flour is coloring too quickly, but keep the pan active enough for browning.
How long should each batch stay in the skillet?
Brown the dredged chicken in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes. The goal at this point is a browned exterior; continue through the remaining pieces in the same way.
The first batch has a light golden coating and no loose wet flour. What should I check before I move on to the next batch?

Check that the browned pieces have an even crust and that the garlic has not scorched. If flour residue is getting too dark in the skillet, lower the heat slightly before adding the next dredged pieces.
I'm making Basil Burgers tonight. The outdoor grill is still cold—what should I get going while I set up?
Preheat the outdoor grill for high heat. Set out a mixing bowl, a spoon or clean hands for combining the meat, and a spatula for turning the patties.
I have 1 1/4 pounds ground beef on the counter. What goes into the bowl with it?

Add 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil (or to taste), 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt, and pepper. Mix only until the seasonings are distributed so the burgers do not get overworked.
The mixture is combined and looks evenly seasoned. How many patties should I make?
Divide it into 4 burger patties. Make them fairly even in thickness so they cook at a similar rate.
The grill is hot now. Do I need to do anything to the grate before the patties go on?
Lightly oil the grill grate, then place the patties on it. Use tongs or a folded paper towel held with tongs to apply the oil safely.
All 4 patties are on the grill and they're starting to sizzle. What timing should I follow?
Cook the burgers about 6 minutes total, turning them once. Keep the lid and heat behavior in mind, but use the thermometer rather than time alone to judge when they are done.
I flipped them once, and the centers are still a little below temperature. What am I looking for before I pull them?
Check the center of a patty with an instant-read thermometer. Cook until the internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), or to the desired doneness indicated by the recipe.
They've reached 160 degrees F and have browned well on both sides. Is there any last texture check?
They should feel set rather than soft in the center, with a browned exterior. Avoid pressing them with the spatula, since that releases their juices.
The burgers are cooked and off the grill. How should I serve them?
Serve the Basil Burgers while hot. If you are using buns or toppings, assemble them just before serving so the patties stay warm and juicy.
Help me stay organized for Fruit Dip 2. What comes first?

Absolutely. This is a chilled dip: blend 8 ounces cream cheese with 1/2 cup marshmallow creme and 2 cups thawed frozen whipped topping, then use unsweetened pineapple juice to loosen it before chilling.
My whipped topping is still partly frozen. Should I wait before mixing?
Yes. Let the 2 cups of whipped topping thaw until it is soft enough to blend smoothly. Starting with thawed topping will keep the dip light rather than lumpy.
What should I put out on the counter while it finishes thawing?
Set out the 8 ounces of cream cheese, 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice. You'll also want a medium mixing bowl and a hand mixer or sturdy spoon for blending.
The cream cheese is soft and the topping has thawed. Do all three main ingredients go in together?
They do. Blend the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and thawed whipped topping together until the mixture is evenly combined and no cream-cheese lumps remain.
It looks thick and fluffy after blending. How do I add the pineapple juice without making it runny?

Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, stirring or blending after each small addition. Stop as soon as the dip is loose enough for fruit to scoop through easily; you may not need every drop of the 1/4 cup.
What texture tells me it is ready to refrigerate?
It should be smooth, creamy, and thick enough to cling to a strawberry or apple slice without falling off in a puddle. If it still feels too dense to dip into, add a little more pineapple juice.
The consistency seems right. Should I cover the bowl?
Yes, cover it and refrigerate for 1 hour. Chilling gives the flavors time to settle and lets the dip firm up slightly.
The hour is almost up, and I'm washing the fruit. Is there anything useful to check before serving?

Give the dip a gentle stir, then check that it is still smooth and scoopable. If it has become firmer than you want, stir in a tiny amount of the remaining pineapple juice only until it returns to dipping consistency.
It is creamy and holds on the fruit nicely. How should I set it out?
Transfer it to a serving bowl and arrange the fruit around it or serve it alongside. Keep the bowl chilled until it is time to eat so the whipped topping stays pleasantly firm.
I'm making Asian Turkey Burgers. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?
Set out a mixing bowl, a spoon or fork for combining, a nonstick skillet, and nonstick cooking spray. Have the turkey ready to add after the other ingredients are mixed.
Which measured ingredients should I put by the bowl?
Measure 1 egg white, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion.
Should I prepare the skillet yet?
You can place the nonstick skillet on the stove, but wait to coat it with nonstick cooking spray until the patties are shaped.
On Asian Turkey Burgers, everything is measured. What goes into the bowl?
Combine the first seven ingredients called for in the recipe in the bowl. Stir the ingredients together so the egg white, soy sauce, bread crumbs, and onion are evenly distributed.
The crumb mixture looks evenly mixed. When do I add the turkey?
Crumble the turkey over the mixture, then mix only until it comes together. Stop once there are no obvious pockets of the crumb mixture; overmixing can make the burgers dense.
It is just combined but still soft. How should I shape it?
Divide the mixture into four portions and gently shape them into four patties. Press only enough to hold each patty together, keeping the thickness fairly even for cooking.
The patties are ready. What should I watch for in the skillet?

Coat the nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray and cook the patties until they are no longer pink. Turn them carefully so they stay intact and check the center of a patty before taking the rest off the stove.
Before I serve them, is there a final check?
Make sure each burger is cooked through with no pink remaining in the center, then transfer the four patties to plates and serve.
I'm making Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me get organized before I start?

Set out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares of unsweetened chocolate, chopped. You'll also want 2 (9 inch) cake pans, a sifter or fine sieve, mixing bowls, and a whisk.
The oven is still cold. What temperature should I use?
Preheat it to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is ready once the batter is prepared.
I have the two 9-inch pans on the counter. How should I prepare them?
Grease and flour both pans, coating the bottoms and sides lightly. Tap out any loose excess flour so it does not leave thick patches on the cake.
Both pans are coated. Should I work on the dry ingredients before touching the chocolate?
Yes. Sift the 2 1/4 cups flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt together into a bowl. The mixture should look evenly combined, with no obvious clumps of baking soda.
A few small flour lumps are caught in my sieve. Is that a problem?
Break up the small lumps with a spoon or whisk them through the sieve. What matters is that the flour, baking soda, and salt are distributed evenly before you set the bowl aside.
The dry mixture is smooth now. What do I do with it?
Set it aside as the recipe directs. Keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate nearby and covered or in its bowl so it is ready for the later chocolate portion of the recipe.
The oven is heating and the pans are ready. Is there anything worth checking before I continue with the remaining directions?

Confirm that the oven has reached 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), both 9-inch pans are greased and floured, and the sifted dry ingredients are set aside. With those pieces ready, you can continue with the next recipe directions without rushing.
Great. I have the flour mixture aside and the 6 ounces of chopped chocolate measured. I'm ready to proceed.

You're in good shape: the dry ingredients have been sifted and set aside, the pans are prepared, and the chocolate is chopped. Follow the remaining cake directions in order, adding the dry mixture when they call for it.
I'm making Baked Apple Oatmeal. Should I get the oven and baking dish ready before I start at the stove?
Yes. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, grease a 2-qt. casserole, and set out a saucepan, spoon, and a cover for the casserole.
Before I continue with Baked Apple Oatmeal, what should I measure for the saucepan?
Measure 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Where do the oats come in?
Keep 2 cups old-fashioned oats ready with the other remaining ingredients. They go in after the milk mixture is heated.
The milk, sugar, butter, salt, and cinnamon are in the saucepan. How should I heat them?
Warm them over medium heat, stirring often, until the sugar dissolves and the butter melts. You want the mixture hot and steamy, not vigorously boiling.
It is hot and smooth now. Can I add the oats?
Yes. Add the oats and the remaining ingredients, then fold them in gently so the mixture stays evenly combined.
The oatmeal mixture looks loose. Is that normal before baking?
It is. The oats will absorb liquid as the casserole bakes. Transfer the mixture to the greased 2-qt. casserole and spread it into an even layer.
It is in the dish. Should it go into the oven uncovered?
Cover the casserole and bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes.
What should I look for when the 45 minutes are up?
The oatmeal should look set around the edges, with most of the liquid absorbed and a soft, spoonable center. Let it stand briefly after baking if it needs a moment to thicken, then serve it warm.
I've got an 11-in. baking dish ready for Baked Fish and Rice 2. What should go into it before it goes in the oven?
Grease the dish, then combine 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth, 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice, 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder.
The broth is boiling and the rice and seasonings are measured. Should I stir it thoroughly before baking?
Yes—stir until the seasonings are distributed through the broth and the rice is evenly submerged. That helps the rice cook uniformly.
What oven temperature should I use, and does the dish need to be covered?
Cover the dish and bake it at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 10 minutes.
The first 10 minutes are nearly up. I thawed and drained the frozen chopped broccoli; what gets added next?
Take the dish out carefully and add the broccoli, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions. Stir them into the rice mixture.
The broccoli is mixed in and the rice is still quite brothy. Should I wait for it to look dry before adding the fish?
No, go ahead while it is still moist. The rice will continue absorbing liquid during the remaining baking time.
How should I arrange the fish fillets?
Lay the fish fillets over the rice mixture in a single layer, then sprinkle them with paprika.
Once the fish is on top, how much longer should the dish bake?
Cover it again and bake for 20 to 25 minutes longer, until the fish flakes easily when pressed with a fork.
The fish is flaking easily and the rice has absorbed most of the broth. Is there anything to add before serving?
Uncover the dish, sprinkle it with cheddar cheese and the remaining onions, then serve while the fish and rice are hot.
I'm making the Crab Quiche. What should I gather before I start?
Set out 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust, 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a large bowl and a whisk.
Should the oven be heating while I prepare the crust?
Yes. Preheat it to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), then place the frozen pie crust where it can go straight into the oven.
How long does the crust bake, and what should it look like?
Bake the crust for about 10 minutes, watching for it to become just starting to brown.
It's beginning to brown now. Do I fill it immediately?
Remove the crust from the oven first and allow it to cool before adding the filling.
While it cools, can I mix the egg filling?
Yes. In a large bowl, whisk together the 4 eggs, 1 cup of heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.
The directions also mention pepper and hot sauce. How much should I use?
The supplied ingredient list gives no amounts for pepper or hot sauce, so don't guess quantities from this recipe excerpt. Use the listed eggs, cream, and salt as the measured mixture.
How do I know when the crust has cooled enough?
It should no longer be hot from the oven before you add the filling. Set it aside while you finish whisking the mixture.
What should I check before pouring anything into the crust?

Confirm that the crust has cooled and that the eggs, cream, and salt are evenly whisked in the bowl. The excerpt provided ends after this filling step, so it does not specify the final baking time or serving instructions.
I'm making Caramel Chocolate Corn and want to get organized before I begin. Which pans and containers should I have ready?

Have cookie sheets ready to grease, a paper bag large enough for the popcorn and peanuts, and a microwave-safe bowl for the caramel mixture. You'll also want a spoon or spatula for combining the bowl ingredients.
I have the cookie sheets out. What ingredients should I measure before I start?
Measure 16 cups popped popcorn, 1 cup roasted peanuts, 1 cup brown sugar, and 1/2 cup butter. Also locate the corn syrup, vanilla, and salt called for in the microwave-bowl instruction.
The popcorn is freshly popped. Should I prepare the sheets or the bag first?
Grease the cookie sheets first, so they are ready when you need them. Then put the popped popcorn and roasted peanuts together in the paper bag.
The sheets are greased, and the popcorn and peanuts are in the bag. Does the bag need anything else right now?
No—set the bag aside as directed. Keep it somewhere stable and away from the microwave work area while you make the mixture.
I'm ready to use the microwave. What goes into the bowl?

In the microwave-safe bowl, combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt. The provided directions do not list amounts for the corn syrup, vanilla, or salt, so use the quantities from your full recipe source if you have them.
Should I add the popcorn to that bowl before microwaving?

Not from the steps you provided. The popcorn and peanuts are meant to remain in the paper bag while the sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt are combined separately in the microwave-safe bowl.
The bowl is combined and the bag is still set aside. What should I check before I continue with the rest of the recipe?

Confirm that the cookie sheets are evenly greased, the bag contains the full popcorn-and-peanut mixture, and the bowl contains all five caramel ingredients. Then continue with the remaining microwave directions from your complete recipe.
Once it's ready to serve, is there anything simple I should look over?
Check that the popcorn and peanuts are coated as intended, that the pieces are not sticking excessively, and that the caramel corn is arranged on the prepared cookie sheets or serving dish neatly.
I have a small saucepan, a deep skillet, and a pastry bag ready for Churros. What should I measure before I start heating anything?

Measure 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, and 1 cup all-purpose flour. Keep the flour within reach, since it goes in after the liquid comes off the heat.
The water, sugar, salt, and vegetable oil are measured. What goes into the saucepan together?
Put the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil into the small saucepan over medium heat. Stir enough to combine as the pan warms.
What am I looking for before I take the saucepan off the burner?
Wait until the mixture reaches a boil, then remove the saucepan from the heat.
It has boiled and I have taken it off the heat. The flour is ready beside me.
Add the flour and stir it in firmly until the mixture forms a ball. It should come together into a single mass rather than remain loose around the sides of the pan.
The dough has formed a ball. Should I set up the frying oil before filling the pastry bag?
Yes. Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). A thermometer is useful here so the oil reaches the stated temperature before the dough goes in.
The oil is approaching 375 degrees F, and the dough is still warm enough to pipe. How should I get it into the pan?
Spoon the dough into the pastry bag, then pipe strips of dough directly into the hot oil. Leave room between the strips so they can fry without sticking together.
The first strips are frying. What should I monitor while they cook?

Keep the frying oil near 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and watch the strips as they cook. They should develop a crisp-looking exterior; avoid crowding the skillet, which can lower the oil temperature.
I am nearly ready to plate them. Is there a useful final check before serving?
Check that the churros have a crisp exterior and that the centers are cooked through. Let excess frying oil drain off briefly, then arrange them for serving while they are hot.
Great, the churros are crisp and ready to serve.
I'm making Broccoli Chicken Roli. What equipment and ingredients should I set out before I begin?

Have ready a large bowl, a cookie sheet, aluminum foil, a drinking glass, and crescent rolls. Set out 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat, 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper.
What else belongs with the chicken and vegetables for the filling?
Measure 1 1/2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese and 1/2 cup mayonnaise. You'll also need mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic for the bowl mixture.
Should I heat the oven before mixing the filling?
Yes—preheat it to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), then line the cookie sheet with aluminum foil while it heats.
The foil-lined sheet is ready. How do I make the filling?
In the large bowl, combine the cooked chicken, fresh broccoli, onion, bell pepper, Cheddar cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic. Mix until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
I've mixed it. What should the mixture look like before I shape the rolls?
The broccoli, chicken, and vegetables should be spread evenly through the creamy mixture, with no pockets of unmixed mayonnaise or seasoning.
How do I arrange the glass and crescent rolls on the prepared sheet?
Place the glass upside down in the center of the cookie sheet. Arrange the crescent rolls around its base with the pointy ends facing away from the glass.
What shape am I aiming for around the glass?
Continue placing the rolls in a circle. Once they surround the glass, the arrangement should resemble the sun, with the pointed ends forming the rays.
Before I move the filled sheet toward the oven, what should I inspect?

Check that the foil still covers the cookie sheet, the glass is centered, and the crescent-roll circle is even with all pointy ends directed outward. Make sure the chicken filling is mixed thoroughly before using it.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV. What equipment should I set out for the tortilla strips?
Use a large pot, a plate lined with paper towels for draining, and a slotted spoon or tongs for lifting out the strips.
I have the pot and paper towels ready. What are the exact ingredients for this part?
Measure 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, cut 6 (6 inch) corn tortillas into 1/2 inch strips, and have 3 cups chicken broth plus 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin nearby.
The tortillas are cut. Should I pour in all of the oil at once?
No. Heat 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat; save the remaining 1/2 teaspoon for the second batch.
The oil is warming. How many strips go in for the first batch?
Add half of the tortilla strips. Stir them often so they crisp evenly rather than browning in one spot.
Some strips are stiffening and turning a little deeper in color. Is that the point to remove them?
Yes—once the first half is crisp, lift the strips out and drain them on the paper towels.
The first batch is draining. What do I do with the oil I held back?
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon oil to the pot, let it heat over medium heat, then fry the remaining tortilla strips the same way, stirring often until crisp.
The second batch is crisp too. Where should the strips go while I continue the soup?
Drain that batch on paper towels as well, then set all the crisp tortilla strips aside. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the next part of the recipe.
Do the tortilla strips need to stay in the pot with the broth?
No. Set the crisp strips aside after draining so they stay crisp for serving rather than sitting in the broth.
I have a Dutch oven out for Adobo Chicken with Ginger. What should I get ready before I turn on the stove?
Set out 1 (3 pound) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces, along with a spoon or ladle for occasional basting. Have the Dutch oven large enough to hold the chicken in the cooking liquid.
The chicken is cut up. Which liquids do I need to measure?
Measure 1/2 cup soy sauce and 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar. Keep both beside the pot so they can go in together with the chicken.
What aromatics belong in the pot with those?
Use 1 bulb garlic, peeled and crushed. Also have the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns ready for the Dutch oven.
Everything is on the counter. Should I start heating the pot before combining it?

Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns in the Dutch oven while the heat is still off. Give the chicken pieces a turn so the seasonings and liquid reach all sides.
The chicken is sitting in the soy-vinegar mixture. What heat should I use?
Put the Dutch oven over medium heat and bring the contents to a boil. Stay nearby as the liquid heats, since the chicken and aromatics may shift as bubbling begins.
I can see active bubbling around the chicken. Do I leave it at medium?
Once it boils, lower the heat to a simmer. You want gentle, steady bubbling rather than a hard boil.
It has settled into a gentle simmer. Should the pot be covered?
Yes. Cover the pot and let the chicken simmer for 30 minutes. During that time, occasionally baste the pieces with the cooking liquid so their exposed surfaces stay coated.
When I baste it, should I move the pieces around too?

A light repositioning is fine if a piece is sitting above the liquid, but keep the pot covered between bastings so the simmer remains steady. Spoon the sauce over the chicken occasionally until the 30 minutes are up.
The 30 minutes are nearly done. What should I check before serving?

Make sure the chicken is cooked through and tender, then spoon some of the adobo liquid over the pieces when serving. The garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns can remain in the pot rather than being plated.
I'm assembling a jar of Double Fudge Brownie Mix. Is this a bake-it-now recipe or a layered mix to give away?
It is a layered dry mix: the recipe directs you to build it in a 1 quart or 1 liter jar, then attach baking instructions on a tag.
Great. I have a clean 1 liter jar. Which ingredient belongs at the bottom?
Start with 2 cups white sugar. Pour it in gently and level the surface so the next layer stays distinct.
The sugar layer is even. What comes directly above it?
Add 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder over the sugar. Spoon it in carefully if you can, since cocoa can puff up and blur the layers.
The cocoa is in, and the jar still has room. What is the third layer?
Layer in 1 cup all-purpose flour next. A flat, even layer will make the jar look neat and keep the listed order clear.
I can see three separate layers. Do the pecans go on top?
Yes. Finish the jar with 1 cup chopped pecans. Leave enough headspace to close the lid securely without crushing them.
The lid is on. What wording from the recipe needs to go on the tag?
The tag should say: "Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C)." Those are the baking directions provided with this mix.
Before I tie on the tag, what should I check on the assembled jar?

Confirm the layers run from bottom to top as white sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, and chopped pecans. Also make sure the jar is sealed and the temperature on the tag reads 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Everything is layered in that order and the tag is readable. Is there anything else required before I put it aside?
That completes the recipe's directions: the dry ingredients are layered in the 1 quart or 1 liter jar, and the preheating instruction is attached.
I'm making Black Bean Chili tonight. What should I chop and measure before I put the saucepan on the heat?
Set a large saucepan near the stove and measure 1 tablespoon olive oil. Chop 1 onion, seed and chop 2 red bell peppers, and seed and mince 1 jalapeno pepper.
I have those vegetables ready. Which of the other produce should I prep while the board is out?
Quarter 10 fresh mushrooms and dice 6 Roma (plum) tomatoes. Have the corn ready as well, along with the black beans, chicken broth, salt, black pepper, cumin, and chili powder.
Everything is prepped. How hot should the pan be for the oil?
Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat. Once it is hot, add the chopped onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn.
The vegetables are in and sizzling. How long should they cook before I season them?
Saute them for 10 minutes, stirring as needed, until the onion is translucent. The peppers and mushrooms should be softened before you add the spices.
The onion has turned translucent and the pan looks less dry. What goes in next?
Season the vegetables with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder, stirring so the spices coat the mixture evenly.
The spices are mixed through. Should I add the beans and liquid together?
Yes. Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Bring the chili to a boil, keeping an eye on the pot so it does not boil over.
It has reached a boil and looks brothy with beans and vegetables throughout. How do I make it thicker?
Carefully remove 1 1/2 cups of the soup and puree that portion in a food processor or blender. Stir the pureed bean mixture back into the saucepan to thicken the chili.
The pureed portion is back in the pot. What should I check before I serve it?
Make sure the texture is evenly thickened, the beans and vegetables are well distributed, and the seasoning is balanced. Once it looks cohesive and hot throughout, it is ready to serve.
I'm getting Cabbage Kielbasa Supper ready in my 5-qt. slow cooker. Can you help me organize the prep?
Set out the slow cooker, a cutting board, and a knife. You'll need 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2-inch cubes, and 1 medium chopped onion.
The cabbage, potatoes, and onion are prepped. What seasonings and liquid belong with them?
Measure 1 3/4 teaspoons salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Also have 1 (14.5-ounce) can of chicken broth ready, along with the kielbasa.
My cooker looks crowded before I've added anything. Is that expected with all the cabbage?
Yes. Add the cabbage, cubed potatoes, chopped onion, salt, and pepper to the 5-qt. slow cooker. It will look quite full at this stage, but the cabbage cooks down.
Those vegetables and seasonings are in. Do I stir in the broth or save it for later?
Pour the chicken broth over the vegetables. A gentle stir is fine to distribute the salt and pepper, but there's no need to pack the cabbage down.
The broth has reached the bottom, and the cabbage is still piled high. Where does the sausage go?
Lay the kielbasa on top of the cabbage. Keep it on the surface rather than trying to force it underneath the vegetables.
Everything is loaded and the lid is on. What cooking setting and timing should I use?
Cook on low for 8 to 9 hours. The supper is ready when the potatoes and cabbage are tender and the sausage is heated through.
If I check near the end, how can I tell whether the potatoes are done without overhandling everything?
Lift the lid briefly and pierce a potato cube with a fork. It should yield easily, and the cabbage should be soft rather than crisp; confirm the kielbasa is hot through as well.
The potatoes are tender, the cabbage has cooked down, and the sausage is hot. Is there anything useful to do before serving?
Give the broth and vegetables a careful stir, then taste the liquid and vegetables for seasoning. Serve once the texture is tender and the sausage is fully heated.
I'm making Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. Can you help me get the oven and mixing setup ready?
Set out a large mixing bowl and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, gather the ingredients so the mixing goes smoothly.
I have the butter and butter flavored shortening on the counter. Which sugars do I need?
Measure 1 cup packed light brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. You'll also use 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening.
Everything measured so far is ready. What belongs together in the large bowl?
Cream the softened butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla together in the large bowl until the mixture is smooth.
I haven't mixed the dry ingredients yet. What should I combine separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Stir that dry mixture into the smooth sugar mixture.
What should the creamed mixture look like before I add the flour mixture?
It should look smooth and evenly blended, without distinct streaks of butter, shortening, or sugar. Once it reaches that point, stir in the combined dry ingredients.
The dry mixture is incorporated. When do the oats and raisins go in?
Stir in the oats and raisins after the flour mixture has been added. Fold them through until they are distributed throughout the dough.
The dough is mixed. Does this recipe say how to portion it onto a baking sheet or how long to bake it?
The directions provided stop after stirring in the oats and raisins, so they do not specify scoop size, baking-sheet spacing, or baking time. Check the complete recipe before portioning and baking.
Once I have the full baking directions, what should I check before serving the cookies?
After baking according to the complete recipe, let the cookies cool enough to handle and check that the texture suits you before serving.
I'm making Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you help me set up the counter before I turn on the broiler?

Set out a medium bowl, spoon or spatula, baking sheet or broiling pan, and the bread. Keep the vegetables nearby: 1 small onion, finely chopped; 1 medium tomato, diced; 1 stalk celery, chopped; and 1 green bell pepper, finely chopped.
I have the onion, tomato, celery, and pepper chopped. What else belongs with them in the bowl?
Add the cheese, chili powder, and salt to the vegetables. Stir everything together until the cheese and seasonings are distributed through the chopped vegetables.
Should I heat the broiler before I put the bread together?
Yes—preheat the oven's broiler now so it is ready once the sandwiches are assembled. Position the bread slices on the baking sheet or broiling pan while it heats.
My mixture looks a little uneven, with more tomato in a few spots. Is that a problem?
Give it another thorough stir, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl. You want each scoop to include vegetables, cheese, chili powder, and salt rather than separate pockets of any ingredient.
How much topping goes on each slice of bread?
Use 1/4 of the mixture per slice. Spread it all the way to the edges so the bread is covered evenly and the topping broils at a similar rate.
The slices are topped. Should the pan go close to the broiler element?
Place the pan under the preheated broiler, leaving enough room that you can safely remove it. Stay nearby, since the cheese can melt and color quickly under direct heat.
What should I look for while they broil?
Broil for 4 to 5 minutes, until the cheese has melted. Look for an evenly hot, melted topping and bread that is beginning to turn crisp around the exposed edges.
They have melted cheese and crisp-looking edges after 5 minutes. Anything to do before serving?
Remove the pan carefully and let the sandwiches sit briefly so the topping settles. Check that each slice is topped to the edges, then serve while the bread is still crunchy.
I'm making Easy Fried Eggplant. Can you help me set up the counter so I can bread and fry the slices without making a mess?

Set out 1 large eggplant, peeled and sliced, along with a shallow dish for 3 beaten eggs and another for 2 cups dry bread crumbs. Keep a plate or tray nearby for the breaded slices, and have paper towels ready for draining after frying.
Should I heat the skillet before I start coating the eggplant?
Yes. Put 2 tablespoons canola oil in a large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat. While it warms, dip each eggplant slice in the beaten egg, then coat it with bread crumbs.
The oil is warming and my first few slices are coated. How will I know the pan is hot enough?
The oil should look fluid and lightly shimmer. Add a breaded slice carefully; it should sizzle on contact without smoking. Leave room between slices so the coating can brown properly.
I have a batch in the skillet. Do I turn them as soon as the crumbs start to color?
Let the first side fry for about 2 to 3 minutes, until it is golden brown, then turn the slices and fry the other side for 2 to 3 minutes as well. Use the color of the crust along with the timing.
One slice is browning faster around the edge than in the middle. What should I do?
If the crumbs are darkening too quickly, lower the heat slightly and give the slice time to color evenly. Turn it once the underside is golden brown rather than repeatedly moving it around.
The first batch looks crisp and golden. Where should I put it while I fry the rest?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels so excess oil can drain away. Keep the pieces in a single layer if possible, which helps the breading stay crisp.
How can I check a piece before serving without overcooking the remaining batches?

Choose one golden slice from the batch, let it cool briefly, and taste it. The coating should be crisp and the eggplant inside should be tender; continue frying the remaining slices for the same 2 to 3 minutes per side, adjusting only if their color changes faster or slower.
Everything is drained and the last slices are golden. Is it ready to bring to the table?
Yes. Serve the fried eggplant while it is hot and crisp after draining on the paper towels. A quick look for an even golden-brown coating and tender centers is the final check.
I'm making Black Bean Lasagna Rolls tonight. Can you help me set up without making it complicated?

Absolutely. Put a large pot of water on for the 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, and have a colander ready. Gather the 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack, 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles, and the black beans.
The water is heating. Should I season it or add oil before the noodles go in?
Cook the noodles according to their package directions, omitting both salt and fat. Once they are tender, drain them thoroughly so excess water does not loosen the filling.
While the noodles cook, what measurements go into the filling bowl?
Stir together the ricotta, Monterey Jack, drained green chiles, 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, and 1/8 teaspoon salt until the mixture is evenly combined.
My noodles are drained and laid out. How much filling should I use?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle, leaving a little room at the edges so the filling stays put when you roll them.
The cheese layer is on. Where do the black beans fit in?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture. Distribute them along each noodle rather than piling them in the center, which will make rolling easier.
How do I tell whether I have filled them too heavily before rolling?

You should still be able to curl each noodle without the beans spilling out. If a noodle looks crowded, shift a few beans to a less-filled one, then roll each noodle up jellyroll fashion from a narrow end.
A couple of rolls are loose at the seam. How should they go into the dish?
Coat an 11- x 7- x 11/2-inch baking dish with cooking spray. Set the rolls in the dish seam-side down; that keeps the loose edges underneath.
Before I move the dish aside, what should I check?

Make sure the rolls are snugly arranged, the seams are all facing down, and no noodle is tearing or leaking a large amount of filling. The drained noodles and evenly spread filling should give you neat, intact rolls.
I'm making Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Before I start, what should I measure and leave within reach?

Set out 1/2 cup margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup molasses, and 1 egg yolk. Have a large bowl ready, plus the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg for the dry mixture.
I have the margarine and sugar in the large bowl. How smooth should the creamed mixture become?
Beat the margarine and sugar together until they look evenly blended and smooth, without visible lumps of margarine around the bowl.
The base is smooth. Should the molasses and yolk go in together?
Yes. Stir in the 1/2 cup molasses and the egg yolk until the mixture is a uniform dark color and the yolk is fully incorporated.
It looks glossy and fairly loose now. What belongs in the dry bowl?

Combine 2 cups sifted all-purpose flour with 1/2 teaspoon salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Mix those dry ingredients together before adding them to the molasses mixture.
My dry ingredients are combined. Should I add them all at once or gradually?
Add the dry mixture to the molasses mixture in portions, stirring as you go. Stop once the dough is smooth and no dry streaks remain; overmixing can make it tougher to roll.
The dough has come together, but it feels soft. Can I roll it right away?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. The rest will firm it up and make rolling the gingerbread men much easier.
The dough is chilling. What should I prepare for shaping and baking once it is firm?
Clear a lightly floured work surface and have your cutters and baking sheets ready. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is hot when the cookies are shaped.
The chilled dough is pliable but no longer sticky. How thin should I roll it?
Roll it on the lightly floured surface to 1/4 inch thickness. If the dough begins sticking, use only enough flour to keep it moving without drying it out.
The shapes are cut and on the sheets. What should I check before they go into the oven?

Make sure the gingerbread men are spaced so their edges will not touch as they bake, and keep the thickness as even as possible. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), checking their texture as they approach doneness rather than relying on an unlisted baking time.
I'm making Carrot Pineapple Cake I. Which pan and oven setting should I get ready before I measure?
Set out a 9x13 inch pan, grease and flour it, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The pan is prepared and the oven is heating. What dry ingredients should I measure into a bowl?
Measure 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon.
Should I combine all of those dry ingredients completely before adding anything else?
Yes. Whisk or stir the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon together so the leavening and seasoning are evenly distributed.
My dry mixture looks even. How do I add the remaining ingredients without making lumps?
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients. Add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into that space, then begin drawing the dry mixture into the wet ingredients.
I have started mixing from the center. What texture am I aiming for?
Use a wooden spoon and mix until the batter is smooth, with no visible pockets of dry flour. Stop once it is combined rather than continuing to stir unnecessarily.
The batter is smooth. Should I scrape it into the prepared 9x13 inch pan now?
Yes. Transfer the batter to the greased and floured pan and spread it into the corners so the surface is reasonably even.
It is in the pan and level. What should I check before it goes into the oven?
Make sure the batter is evenly settled in the pan and that the oven has reached 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Then place the pan on an oven rack to bake.
Once it has baked, what should I look for before serving the cake?
Let the cake cool enough to handle, then check that the texture is set before slicing. Cut and serve from the 9x13 inch pan when it has cooled to your preferred serving temperature.

Start by preparing 1 cup torn corn bread; 2/3 cup hot water. Leave these items clearly organized so the next addition stays unambiguous.

I'm getting ready to make Country Fried Chicken. What can I measure out before handling the chicken?
Set out the dry coating ingredients: 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika. Have a large resealable plastic bag and a shallow bowl ready too.
Should the garlic salt, pepper, and paprika go into the flour now?
Yes. Combine the flour with the 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika for the seasoned flour mixture.
I have the seasoned flour mixed. Where should I put it?
Put it in the large resealable plastic bag. The written directions describe this as combining the first five ingredients in that bag.
What do I prepare separately for the wet coating?
In a shallow bowl, beat the egg and milk together until they are blended.
The egg and milk are ready. Can I start breading the chicken?
Add the chicken to the bag a few pieces at a time, then shake the bag so each piece gets coated with the seasoned flour.
Some pieces have flour on them, but the coating is still dry. What comes next?
Take each floured piece through the egg-and-milk mixture, making sure the surface is moistened.
After the egg mixture, do the pieces go straight back into the bag?
They do. Return them to the flour mixture and shake again for the second coating.
How can I tell when the breading step is complete?

Each piece should have a visible, fairly even second layer of seasoned flour after the egg dip. Once they are coated, the breading directions in this recipe excerpt are complete; use the remaining cooking directions from your full recipe for frying and serving.
For the British Bread Pudding, let's use the first crunchy-topping version we talked about earlier.
Understood—I'll use the first of those topping options for this British Bread Pudding and keep the rest of the cooking on track.
Yes, exactly. I don't want to reopen that choice tonight; please just guide me through the pudding.
Absolutely. That topping choice is settled for this batch.
I'm clearing the counter. What ingredients should I measure out?

Set out 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread, 1 1/4 cups milk, 1 beaten egg, and 1/3 cup softened butter. Have 3/4 cup raisins ready too, along with the mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon called for in your recipe.
Should I get the oven and bakeware ready before I start soaking the bread?
Yes. Heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), and have a 9-inch square baking pan nearby.
The bread and milk are in my large bowl. How long do they sit?
Let the bread soak in the 1 1/4 cups milk for 5 minutes. This gives the cubes time to soften before the richer ingredients go in.
The 5 minutes are up, and the bread is soft but still has a little shape. What do I add?
Stir in the beaten egg, the 1/3 cup softened butter, the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Work through the bowl so the additions are spread evenly.
It is a thick, fruit-studded mixture now. When does the topping choice come in?
Once the pudding mixture is evenly combined, use the first crunchy-topping version you chose earlier. Keep that same version rather than switching to the other one.
My 9-inch square pan is ready. Should I pack the mixture down hard?

Press the mixture into the 9-inch square pan evenly, but don't compress it aggressively. The recipe's final mixing instruction is simply to mix well, so aim for an even distribution of bread, fruit, and spices.
Before I put it in the oven, what should I check?

Make sure there are no pockets of unmixed egg or softened butter and that the fruit and spices are dispersed throughout. Your instructions provide the 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) oven setting, but no baking duration, so use any baking-time direction on your recipe card rather than guessing one.

Before I handle the next part of Garlic Chicken Stir Fry, how do I tell that this part is settled?

I'm making Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes tonight. Can you guide me as I cook it?

Absolutely. Gather the Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini, and dried basil. A soup pot, spoon, knife, cutting board, and can opener will be useful.
I have everything out. How should I prep the zucchini before I start heating the soup?
Dice the 2 medium zucchini into bite-size pieces so they can become tender in the same pot as the tortellini. Open the tomatoes and measure 1 tsp. dried basil so it is ready to add.
The zucchini is diced, and I've prepared the Fast Chicken Soup Base in my pot. What heat am I aiming for?
Bring the chicken soup base to a simmer. You want small, steady bubbles rather than a hard boil.
It is simmering gently now. Should all of the remaining ingredients go in together?

Yes. Add the 1 9-ounce package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and the 1 tsp. dried basil. Stir gently so the tortellini separates in the broth.
Everything is in, and the tortellini is starting to move around the pot. How long should it cook?
Keep the soup at a simmer for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. Stir occasionally, especially during the first few minutes, to keep the tortellini from sticking together.
I'm at about 10 minutes. The zucchini is softer, but I'm not sure whether the tortellini is done.

Taste one tortellini and check a piece of zucchini. The tortellini should be tender throughout, and the zucchini should yield easily without turning mushy. If either needs more time, continue simmering and check again within the remaining 20-minute window.
Both are tender now, and the soup looks ready. Is there anything to check before I ladle it out?
Give it a final stir and taste the broth for overall balance. Make sure the tortellini is tender and the zucchini is cooked through, then turn off the heat.
The texture is where I want it. Should I let it sit before serving?
You can serve it right away. Ladle the Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes into bowls, making sure each serving gets broth, tortellini, tomatoes, and zucchini.
